Welcoming Relatives: Family members and friends, including grandmother, grandfather, aunt, uncle, and cousins, came to meet the new babies.

q_and_a.question: A family tree connects different generations living together. Based on the chapter, explain the structure of a large family and describe how each member relates to the child ('Me').
q_and_a.answer: The chapter illustrates a large family structure organized across three generations: 1. The First Generation (Grandparents): - Grandfather: The father of one's father or mother. He shares stories, reads, and guides the family. - Grandmother: The mother of one's father or mother. She sings songs, prepares meals, and cares lovingly for the children. 2. The Second Generation (Parents, Uncles, and Aunts): - Father: The male parent who works, provides food, and eats meals with the child. - Mother: The female parent who nurtures, plays, and takes care of the household. - Uncle: The brother of the father or mother who plays with and helps the family. - Aunt: The sister of the father or mother, or the wife of the uncle, who shares duties and loves the children. 3. The Third Generation (Children, Siblings, and Cousins): - Brother: The male sibling with whom the child dances, plays, and learns. - Sister: The female sibling who participates in games, decorations, and studies. - Cousin: The child of an uncle or aunt who acts as a playful friend and companion. - Me: The child who is loved, protected, and supported by all these family members. Conclusion: In an Indian family, all three generations live together with mutual respect, cooperation, and love.

q_and_a.question: Discuss the roles and relationships shown in the songs 'My Family' and 'The Family Song', and explain why living in a family is special.
q_and_a.answer: Both poems in the chapter celebrate the bond of love and togetherness among family members: 1. Activities Shared with Family Members in 'My Family': - Mother: Plays games and shares happy moments with the child. - Father: Sits and eats meals together, sharing food. - Brother and Sister: Dance and have fun together as companions. - Grandmother: Sings sweet songs and melodies with the child. - Grandfather: Reads books and stories together with the child. 2. Features of 'The Family Song': - Size of Family: It describes a large joint family of ten members. - Relations: It includes mother, father, brother, sister, uncle, aunt, cousin, grandfather, and grandmother. - Togetherness: All the members eat meals together and play together. - Affection: Every member shows love and care, staying happily under one roof. 3. Why Family is Special: - A family provides safety, care, and food to every child. - Family members help each other in daily work. - Sharing activities like reading, singing, and playing creates lifelong love and happiness.

q_and_a.question: Describe the complete journey of the sparrow family from building their nest to the day the babies flew into the sky.
q_and_a.answer: The story 'The Sparrow Family' describes the life of a bird family through the following stages: 1. Building a Safe Home: - Mama and Papa sparrow found a safe and quiet branch on a leafy tree. - Together, they made a little nest that was warm and soft to live in. 2. The Arrival of the Eggs: - Mama sparrow laid three small eggs in the cozy nest. - The parents kept the eggs safe and warm. 3. The Birth of the Chicks: - One day, the eggs broke open. - Three little heads popped out into the world. 4. Caring for the Young Ones: - Papa sparrow worked hard and brought food for the hungry babies. - Both parents protected and nurtured the chicks. 5. Visit from Relatives and Friends: - Grandfather sparrow and Grandmother sparrow came to visit. - Aunt sparrow, Uncle sparrow, cousins, and friends all came together to see the babies. 6. Growing Up and Flying: - The baby sparrows ate well and grew bigger and bigger. - Finally, one day, they hopped out of the nest and flew high up into the big blue sky.

During discussion, the teacher asks questions to help learners answer, using their mother tongue if needed.

q_and_a.question: How did the cap-seller get his caps back from the monkeys? Explain the events in sequence.
q_and_a.answer: The cap-seller got his caps back through clever thinking: 1. When the cap-seller woke up and saw that the monkeys had taken his caps, he shook his fists at them. The monkeys imitated him and shook their fists too. 2. Next, the cap-seller scratched his head. The monkeys copied his action and scratched their heads as well. 3. Seeing that the monkeys were copying him, the cap-seller had an idea. He took off his own cap and threw it into the empty basket. 4. The monkeys did the exact same thing and threw their caps down. 5. The cap-seller collected all his caps back into the basket and went away happily.

q_and_a.question: Describe the conversation between the frog and the crow in the story 'The Frog and the Crow'. What happened at the end?
q_and_a.answer: In the story 'The Frog and the Crow', the conversation and events happened as follows: 1. The proud frog asked the crow if he could swim like him. The crow replied that he could not. 2. Next, the frog asked if the crow could jump like him. The crow again replied that he could not. 3. The frog then boasted that since the crow could neither jump nor swim, what could he actually do? 4. The crow politely agreed with the frog and said that while he could not jump or swim, he could walk and fly. 5. At the end, the crow proved his ability by flying away, catching the proud frog in its beak.

q_and_a.question: Compare and contrast the two stories given in the chapter: 'The Frog and the Crow' and 'The Cap-seller and the Monkeys'. Focus on the characters, the central problem, the actions taken, and the final outcomes.
q_and_a.answer: A detailed comparison of both stories from the chapter is as follows: 1. Characters: - 'The Frog and the Crow' features two animal characters: a proud frog who lived in a pond and a clever crow who lived in a tree. - 'The Cap-seller and the Monkeys' features a human cap-seller who traveled to sell caps and a group of mischievous monkeys living in a tree. 2. Central Problem: - In the first story, the problem arises from the frog's excessive pride and arrogance. The frog looked down upon the crow because the crow could not swim or jump. - In the second story, the problem is a practical loss. The cap-seller lost his merchandise because the monkeys stole all the caps from his basket while he was asleep. 3. Actions Taken: - In 'The Frog and the Crow', the frog continuously questioned and insulted the crow's abilities. The crow remained calm, stated what he could do (walk and fly), and then acted swiftly. - In 'The Cap-seller and the Monkeys', the man tried shaking his fists and scratching his head. When he noticed the monkeys imitating him, he used his intelligence to throw his own cap into the basket. 4. Outcomes: - In 'The Frog and the Crow', pride led to the frog's downfall. The crow flew away, catching the proud frog in its beak. - In 'The Cap-seller and the Monkeys', patience and clever thinking saved the man. The monkeys threw down their caps, and the cap-seller recovered all his goods happily. 5. Main Lessons: - 'The Frog and the Crow' teaches that pride and boasting can lead to harm, and we should never underestimate others. - 'The Cap-seller and the Monkeys' teaches that wit, calm thinking, and observation can overcome tricky troubles.

q_and_a.question: Give a complete account of the story 'The Cap-seller and the Monkeys' from beginning to end. What does this story teach us about handling difficult situations?
q_and_a.answer: The story 'The Cap-seller and the Monkeys' unfolds as follows: 1. Introduction: There was a man who sold caps for a living. He carried many colorful caps in a large basket on his head. 2. The Incident: One day, feeling tired, the cap-seller took rest and slept under the cool shade of a big tree. While he was fast asleep, monkeys living on the tree climbed down, took all the caps from his basket, and climbed back up, wearing them. 3. The Discovery: When the cap-seller woke up, he was shocked to find his basket empty. He looked around and looked above into the branches. He saw all the monkeys wearing his caps. 4. Trying to Solve the Problem: The cap-seller shook his fists in anger, but the monkeys merely copied him and shook their fists. Then he scratched his head in confusion, and the monkeys imitated him by scratching their heads too. 5. The Clever Plan: Observing the monkeys' habit of copying human actions, the cap-seller had a brilliant idea. He took off the cap from his own head and threw it down into the empty basket. 6. The Conclusion: The monkeys followed his action immediately and threw all their caps down into the basket. The cap-seller collected all his caps and went away happily. 7. Lesson Learned: This story teaches us that when we face a difficult or stressful situation, getting angry does not help. Instead, staying calm, observing the surroundings carefully, and using our presence of mind helps us solve the problem easily.

Explain: (a) How can you make five new rhyming words ending with 'at'? (b) What are the action words given in the lesson that a teacher asks students to perform?
q_and_a.answer: (a) By adding letters to 'at', we can make the following five rhyming words: 1. C + at = Cat 2. M + at = Mat 3. F + at = Fat 4. R + at = Rat 5. H + at = Hat (b) The action words given in the lesson are: 1. Catch (e.g., Catch the ball) 2. Throw (e.g., Throw the ball) 3. Hide (e.g., Hide under a table) 4. Open (e.g., Open your pencil box or bag) 5. Close (e.g., Close your pencil box or bag) 6. Say (e.g., Say hurray!)

q_and_a.question: Describe the conversation and the chase between the cat and the rat in the story 'Catch me if you can'.
q_and_a.answer: The story 'Catch me if you can' tells of a playful chase between a cat and a rat: 1. First Challenge: A fat cat was sitting on a mat. She challenged the little rat, saying, 'I can catch you, little rat.' 2. The Rat's First Escape: The little rat saw the cat and hid inside a hat. The rat replied bravely, 'No, no, you can't.' 3. The Chase: Hearing this, the cat ran fast to catch the rat. 4. The Rat's Second Escape: The clever rat ran quickly and hid inside a box. 5. The Ending: The lid of the box did not open. The safe rat laughed and said, 'Ha, ha! You can't catch me, big cat!'

q_and_a.question: Read the story 'Catch me if you can' and answer the following questions: (a) Which animals are there in the story? (b) Where was the cat sitting at first? (c) What did the cat say to the little rat? (d) Where did the rat hide first? (e) Why was the cat unable to catch the rat in the end?
q_and_a.answer: Based on the story 'Catch me if you can', the answers are: (a) The two animals in the story are a cat and a rat. (b) At first, the fat cat sat on a mat. (c) The cat said, 'I can catch you, little rat.' (d) The rat first hid in a hat after seeing the cat. (e) The cat could not catch the rat because the rat ran and hid inside a box, and the lid of the box did not open.

q_and_a.question: The poem 'Let us sing and enjoy a song' introduces children to many everyday objects and sounds in nature and the classroom environment. (a) Write the lines of the poem that describe nature, play, and household objects. (b) List all the pairs of rhyming words used in the poem. (c) What message does the poem give to young learners about learning from things around them?
q_and_a.answer: (a) Description of Objects in the Poem: 1. Nature and Living Things: The poem mentions a green tree, a flower, and a buzzing bee. 2. Moving Objects: A car that goes by fast and loud, and a kite flying high above the cloud. 3. Personal Items and Toys: A ball rolling by a little shoe, a red and blue hat, and a bottle filled with water to sip. 4. Study and Rest Objects: A book that can be turned and flipped, a chair to rest on, and a clock that makes a ticking sound. (b) Rhyming Words in the Poem: 1. see - bee 2. loud - cloud 3. shoe - blue 4. sip - flip 5. ticks - clicks (c) Message to Young Learners: The poem shows children that English is all around them in their everyday environment. By observing simple objects at home, at school, and on the road—such as shoes, bottles, books, clocks, and trees—learning becomes interesting, natural, and enjoyable. When children connect words to real objects, learning truly clicks!

q_and_a.question: Write a complete summary of the story 'Catch me if you can' and explain the comprehension questions given after the story with their answers.
q_and_a.answer: Summary of 'Catch me if you can': A fat cat was sitting on a mat. She saw a little rat and said, 'I can catch you, little rat.' Hearing this, the little rat hid inside a hat and replied, 'No, no, you can't.' The cat then ran to catch the rat. The clever rat ran away quickly and hid inside a box. The cat tried to get the rat, but the lid of the box did not open. Safe inside, the rat teased the cat by saying, 'Ha, ha! You can't catch me, big cat!' Comprehension Questions and Answers from the text: 1. Which animals are there in this story? Answer: A cat and a rat are the two animals in this story. 2. Who sat on the mat? Answer: A fat cat sat on the mat. 3. 'I can catch you, little rat' - who said this? Answer: The cat said these words. 4. Where did the rat hide? Answer: The rat first hid in a hat and then hid inside a box. 5. Was the lid of the box open? Answer: No, the lid of the box was not open.

q_and_a.question: What colour is the pigeon?
q_and_a.answer: The pigeon is grey in colour.

q_and_a.question: What colour is the crow?
q_and_a.answer: The crow is black in colour.

q_and_a.question: What does the cow eat?
q_and_a.answer: The cow eats grass.

q_and_a.question: Where does the dog live near Jaggu's house?
q_and_a.answer: The dog lives near the gate.

q_and_a.question: Where does Jaggu live?
q_and_a.answer: Jaggu lives in Nagpur.

q_and_a.question: What animals did Jeje have on his farm?
q_and_a.answer: Jeje had some cats on his farm.

q_and_a.question: What sound did the hen make on the farm?
q_and_a.answer: The hen made a cluck-cluck sound.

q_and_a.question: What sound did the cow make on the farm?
q_and_a.answer: The cow made a moo-moo sound.

q_and_a.question: Who had a farm in the song?
q_and_a.answer: Grandpa had a farm.

q_and_a.question: What does the text say about an elephant?
q_and_a.answer: An elephant has one trunk and two eyes.

q_and_a.question: Describe the colour and beak of the parrot.
q_and_a.answer: The parrot is green in colour and has a red beak.

q_and_a.question: Why must one walk carefully in the field beside Jaggu's house?
q_and_a.answer: One must walk carefully because there are a few snakes in the field.

q_and_a.question: What do the monkeys do in the trees?
q_and_a.answer: The monkeys swing and jump in the trees.

q_and_a.question: What does the cat do to the small rat?
q_and_a.answer: The cat chases the small rat.

q_and_a.question: What do the cats do in the verandah?
q_and_a.answer: The cats jump up and down in the verandah of Jaggu's house.

q_and_a.question: What important lessons about nature, animals, and birds do students learn from this chapter? Explain with examples from Jaggu's description and the rhymes.
q_and_a.answer: From Chapter 4, students learn several valuable lessons about animals and nature: 1. Identifying Domestic and Farm Animals: Students learn to recognise common animals such as cows, dogs, cats, hens, goats, and pigs, as well as the unique sounds they make like 'moo-moo', 'cluck-cluck', and 'mew-mew'. 2. Observing Birds and Colours: Through Jaggu's words, children learn how to identify birds by their features and colours, such as the black crow, grey pigeon, green parrot with a red beak, and multi-coloured peacock. 3. Being Cautious in Nature: Jaggu reminds us that some creatures like snakes live in open fields, so we must always walk carefully and watch our step. 4. Love and Kindness Towards Animals: The 'Mental Talk' section gives the central message: 'Animals and birds are our friends. Love them.' We should live peacefully with animals, feed them, and treat them with care.

q_and_a.question: What animals and sounds are mentioned in the rhymes 'A Farm' and 'Let's sing and enjoy'? Explain how they are described.
q_and_a.answer: The rhymes in the lesson describe a grandfather's farm and the animals living there: 1. Cow: Grandpa has a cow on his farm. The cow makes a 'moo-moo' sound here, there, and everywhere. 2. Hen: Grandpa also has a hen on his farm. The hen makes a 'cluck-cluck' sound all around the farm. 3. Cats: In the song about Jeje's farm, there are cats. The cats make a sweet 'mew, mew' sound everywhere on the farm.

q_and_a.question: Write about the different birds mentioned by Jaggu in the lesson along with their features.
q_and_a.answer: Jaggu sees different kinds of birds near his house and describes them as follows: 1. Crow: The crow is black in colour. 2. Pigeon: The pigeon is grey in colour. 3. Sparrow: The sparrow is described as a small bird. 4. Parrot: The parrot is green in colour and has a bright red beak. 5. Peacock: The peacock is a beautiful bird that has many colours.

q_and_a.question: Describe the animals that Jaggu sees near his house and what they do.
q_and_a.answer: In the lesson, Jaggu tells us about several animals that live near his house: 1. Dog: The dog lives near the gate of his house. 2. Cats: The cats jump up and down in the verandah of his house. They also chase rats. 3. Cow: There is a cow that eats green grass under a shed. 4. Rat: Jaggu sees a very small rat that gets chased by a cat. 5. Monkeys: The monkeys swing and jump happily in the trees. 6. Snakes: There are a few snakes in the field beside his house, so one must walk carefully there.

q_and_a.question: Explain all the different activities, rhymes, and exercises presented in Chapter 4 'A farm'.
q_and_a.answer: Chapter 4, titled 'A farm', includes several engaging learning sections for Class 3 students: 1. Pre-listening Activity: Students look at pictures of domestic animals and birds like dogs, cows, parrots, goats, pigs, pigeons, hens, and cats. They practice a chain-drill sentence: 'I have a dog. It's name is Titu. What's about you?' 2. While-listening Rhyme ('A Farm'): A musical rhyme about a grandfather who has a farm ('E-I-E-I-O'). It teaches children the animals and their sounds, specifically a cow that goes 'moo-moo' and a hen that goes 'cluck-cluck'. 3. Post-listening Activities: - Visual Memory Development Technique (VMDT): Children close their eyes, recall pictures, and locate specific animals like the cat, pigeon, goat, pig, hen, cow, and dog. - Let us listen and speak: Another rhyme about 'Jeje' who has cats on his farm that make the sound 'mew, mew'. 4. Let us read ('Animals and Birds'): A reading passage where Jaggu from Nagpur describes the animals (dog, cats, cow, rat, monkeys, snakes) and birds (crow, pigeon, sparrow, parrot, peacock) around his house. 5. Let us write: - A colouring activity where learners identify and write names of farm animals using a help box (Cat, Cow, Goat, Pig, Hen, Cock, Sparrow). - A question-answer dialogue identifying colours of birds and animals. - A handwriting exercise about an elephant having one trunk and two eyes. 6. Mental Talk and Creative Task: A moral thought stating 'Animals and birds are our friends. Love them', followed by a drawing box where children draw their favourite pets.

q_and_a.question: Give a complete description of the story 'Animals and Birds' narrated by Jaggu. Mention who Jaggu is, where he lives, and detail all the animals and birds he sees around his house.
q_and_a.answer: Introduction: The story 'Animals and Birds' is told by a young boy named Jaggu. He lives in Nagpur and invites us to learn about the different animals and birds that live around his home. Animals near Jaggu's house: 1. Dog: A faithful dog lives right near the front gate of his house. 2. Cats: Two playful cats jump up and down in the verandah of the house. They also chase after small rats. 3. Rat: A very small rat is seen running around, trying to escape from the cat. 4. Cow: A gentle cow stays near the house and eats fresh green grass. 5. Monkeys: A group of monkeys stay in the big trees, where they swing and jump from branch to branch. 6. Snakes: In the open field right beside Jaggu's house, there are a few snakes. Jaggu warns everyone to walk carefully in the field. Birds near Jaggu's house: 1. Crow: A crow that is black in colour. 2. Pigeon: A pigeon that is grey in colour. 3. Sparrow: A tiny, gentle bird called a sparrow. 4. Parrot: A lovely green parrot with a bright red beak. 5. Peacock: A large and attractive peacock that has feathers of many different colours. Conclusion: Jaggu concludes by saying that he loves all animals and birds, showing that they are our friends and we must care for them.

q_and_a.question: Why should we eat vegetables every day?
q_and_a.answer: We should eat vegetables every day because they are good for our health.

q_and_a.question: What does Mini hold in her hand while returning home from the market?
q_and_a.answer: Mini holds a small basket of flowers in her hand.

q_and_a.question: What is the name of the big green fruit kept on the left of the apples?
q_and_a.answer: The big green fruit kept on the left of the apples is a watermelon.

q_and_a.question: What are the large fruits kept behind the apples in the market?
q_and_a.answer: The large fruits kept behind the apples are pineapples.

q_and_a.question: Name two flowers that Mini and her father see in the market.
q_and_a.answer: They see roses and marigolds in the market.

q_and_a.question: On which day does Mini go to the market with her father?
q_and_a.answer: Mini goes to the market with her father every Sunday.

q_and_a.question: What does Mini's father do for a living?
q_and_a.answer: Mini's father is a farmer.

q_and_a.question: How many apples are hanging on the tree in the poem?
q_and_a.answer: There are five red apples hanging on the tree.

q_and_a.question: What is the colour of the mangoes hanging on the tree in the song?
q_and_a.answer: The mangoes hanging on the tree are yellow in colour.

q_and_a.question: When is Pakhala Divas celebrated every year in our state?
q_and_a.answer: Pakhala Divas is celebrated on 20th March every year.

q_and_a.question: How do the students prepare a fruit chaat in class?
q_and_a.answer: Each student brings a fruit to class and washes it well. The teacher cuts the fruits and helps the children prepare the fruit chaat to eat together.

q_and_a.question: What does Mini's mother sometimes make with jasmine flowers?
q_and_a.answer: Mini's mother sometimes makes a string of jasmine flowers.

q_and_a.question: What things do people buy in the market?
q_and_a.answer: People in the market buy vegetables and fruits. They also buy flowers and toys.

q_and_a.question: What do the squirrel and the rabbit do around the fruit tree?
q_and_a.answer: The squirrel runs up the tree. The rabbit lives under the tree.

q_and_a.question: Who rests under the tree and who rests on the tree in the song 'Fruits for All'?
q_and_a.answer: A traveller rests under the shade of the tree. A bird rests on the tree.

q_and_a.question: Based on the chapter, describe the picture exercise where picture words complete the story about visiting the market, and explain what we learn from Mental Talk.
q_and_a.answer: The chapter includes a reading exercise and an important health lesson: 1. The Story with Pictures: - Today, my father took me to the market. - I saw many fruits and vegetables there. - I liked the oranges. - My father bought me an apple. - We bought potatoes and onion. - We had a good dinner. 2. Mental Talk Message: - The lesson reminds us that vegetables are very good for our health. - We should eat fresh vegetables every day to remain fit and strong. - The teacher also discusses that food is valuable, so we must never waste food.

q_and_a.question: Describe the conversation between Mini and her father about the flowers and fruits they see in the market.
q_and_a.answer: Mini and her father have a pleasant conversation as they walk through the market: 1. Flowers: Mini points out the colourful flowers. Her father tells her the names of the flowers, pointing out roses, marigolds, and jasmine flowers. Mini happily adds that her mother sometimes makes a string of jasmine flowers at home. 2. Fruits: Next, her father shows her the fruit section. Mini sees apples and asks about the large fruits kept behind them. Her father tells her they are pineapples. 3. More Fruits: Mini asks about the fruits placed to the right of the apples, and her father explains that they are oranges. She then asks about the big green fruit on the left, and her father identifies it as a watermelon.

q_and_a.question: Write about the song 'Fruits for All'. Mention how many fruits are on the trees and who receives each fruit.
q_and_a.answer: The song 'Fruits for All' talks about sharing fruits from the trees. 1. In the first part of the song, there are five yellow mangoes hanging on the tree. 2. In the second part, there are five red apples hanging on another tree. 3. The fruits are shared lovingly among different friends: - One fruit is for the traveller who rests under the shade of the tree. - One fruit is for the bird who rests or nests on the tree. - One fruit is for the playful squirrel who runs up the tree. - One fruit is for the rabbit who lives under the tree. - One fruit is for you to share with me. Through this song, children learn that nature gives food to all living beings and that sharing brings joy.

q_and_a.question: What happens when Mini goes to the market with her father? Describe their visit and the things they bring back home.
q_and_a.answer: Mini goes to the market with her father every Sunday. 1. Mini's father is a farmer. He grows fresh vegetables on his farm and takes them to the market to sell. 2. In the market, her father sells his vegetables and takes Mini around to show her different shops. 3. Mini sees many people buying fruits, vegetables, flowers, and toys. 4. Together, they look at lovely flowers like roses, marigolds, and jasmines, as well as fruits like pineapples, oranges, and a watermelon. 5. After their visit, Mini returns home holding a small basket of flowers in her hand, while her father carries a bag of fruits.

q_and_a.question: Describe all the activities given in the chapter, including the pre-reading meal, the question-and-answer exercises, handwriting practice, and the classroom fruit chaat activity.
q_and_a.answer: The chapter provides a rich variety of interactive activities that build observation, speaking, writing, and sharing habits among Class 3 pupils: 1. Pre-reading Activity: - Children look at the picture of an Odia meal with a large bowl of Pakhala (fermented rice) served with fried fish, potatoes, leafy greens, onions, and lemon. - Children learn that Pakhala Divas is celebrated every year on 20th March in Odisha. 2. Visual Memory Development Technique (VMDT) and Picture Observation: - Pupils look at groups of fruits and vegetables with their 'eye camera'. - They place their index finger on yellow fruits and white vegetables. - They answer questions identifying red fruits, green vegetables, and the number of items shown. 3. Listening and Speaking Activities: - Chain Drill: Children recite the song 'Fruits for All' line by line in turns. - Role Play: Students pair up to act as Mini and her father, reading out the dialogue about flowers in the market. 4. Reading and Writing Activities: - Handwriting Practice: Pupils write descriptive phrases on four-line guides, such as 'yellow mango', 'red apple', 'yellow banana', 'green guava', 'purple brinjal', 'brown potato', 'orange carrot', and 'white radish'. - Picture Questions (Yes/No Practice): Pupils complete sentences using 'Yes, they are' or 'No, they are not' to name tomatoes, carrots, marigolds, potatoes, oranges, and cabbages. - Creative Expression: Children draw and colour their favourite fruit and vegetable in a drawing box and talk about why they like them. 5. Classroom Group Activity ('Let us do'): - Each child brings one fruit to school from home. - The pupils wash their fruits properly and hand them to the teacher. - The teacher cuts the fruits and helps them prepare a delicious fruit chaat. - All the children sit together in a circle, share the fruit chaat, and enjoy eating as a class.

q_and_a.question: Provide a complete account of the fruits, vegetables, and flowers featured in the chapter. Mention their colours, how they are described, and explain what the teacher notes encourage the students to do.
q_and_a.answer: The chapter introduces young learners to many common fruits, vegetables, and flowers through pictures, stories, and activities. 1. Flowers Mentioned: - Roses: Beautiful red and colourful flowers seen in the market. - Marigolds: Bright yellow and orange flowers. - Jasmine: Sweet-smelling flowers that Mini's mother uses to make flower strings. 2. Fruits Mentioned and Their Colours: - Mango: Yellow fruit hanging on the tree. - Apple: Bright red fruit hanging on the tree and displayed in the shop. - Orange: Round, orange-coloured fruit placed to the right of the apples. - Pineapple: Large fruit with rough skin kept behind the apples. - Watermelon: Big green fruit kept to the left of the apples. - Other fruits shown include bananas (yellow), guavas (green), grapes, and jackfruit. 3. Vegetables Mentioned and Their Colours: - Brinjal: Purple vegetable. - Potato: Brown vegetable used in daily meals. - Carrot: Orange vegetable grown on the farm. - Radish: White vegetable with green leaves. - Tomato: Bright red vegetable. - Cauliflower: Creamy-white vegetable. - Cabbage: Leafy green vegetable. - Peas: Small green vegetables inside pods. - Onion: Red-purple vegetable commonly used for cooking. 4. Teacher Guidance and Learning Points: - Teachers encourage students to name these items in English and in their home language. - Students learn to observe colours and identify which fruits are yellow or red, and which vegetables are white or green. - Children are guided to understand that vegetables and fruits keep our bodies healthy and that food must never be wasted.

q_and_a.question: I am hard and brown on the outside, and soft and white inside. Who am I?
q_and_a.answer: It is a coconut.

q_and_a.question: Which fruit shares its name with its colour?
q_and_a.answer: The fruit is an orange.

q_and_a.question: Give two examples of one-syllable words listed in the chapter.
q_and_a.answer: Two examples of one-syllable words are 'man' and 'cat'.

q_and_a.question: Where was all the food when Mummy returned home?
q_and_a.answer: All the food was in the gorilla's tummy.

q_and_a.question: Who came to the house one day in the story?
q_and_a.answer: A big gorilla came to the house one day.

q_and_a.question: According to the poem 'I like food', who gives us good food?
q_and_a.answer: God gives us all good food.

q_and_a.question: Why did one girl in the park have no food?
q_and_a.answer: She had no food because her mother was sick.

q_and_a.question: Where are the teacher and pupils in Picture 1?
q_and_a.answer: The teacher and pupils are in a nearby park.

q_and_a.question: Write the rhyming words from the poem 'I like food' for 'favours' and 'yummy'.
q_and_a.answer: The word that rhymes with 'favours' is 'flavours', and the word that rhymes with 'yummy' is 'tummy'.

q_and_a.question: Why should we say 'thank you' to farmers?
q_and_a.answer: We should say thank you to farmers because they work hard in the fields to grow many kinds of food for us to eat.

q_and_a.question: What two things do we get from cows according to the reading activity?
q_and_a.answer: We get milk from cows, and from that milk, we make curds and butter.

q_and_a.question: Divide the words 'farmer' and 'dinner' into their syllables.
q_and_a.answer: The word 'farmer' divides into far-mer, and 'dinner' divides into din-ner.

q_and_a.question: Name three things the gorilla ate at the house.
q_and_a.answer: The gorilla ate bananas, biscuits, and apples at the house.

q_and_a.question: Why should we not waste food according to the poem?
q_and_a.answer: We should not waste food because all foods are blessings given to us by God.

q_and_a.question: How did the two boys help the girl who had no food?
q_and_a.answer: One boy offered to share his paratha, and the other boy offered his chakuli. Both kindly shared their lunch with her.

q_and_a.question: Solve the four riddles given in the chapter and describe each item based on its clues.
q_and_a.answer: 1. Riddle (a): - Clue: 'I am a fruit. My name is my colour. Who am I?' - Answer: Orange. It is a citrus fruit named after its orange color. 2. Riddle (b): - Clue: 'I am hard and brown on the outside. Soft and white inside. Who am I?' - Answer: Coconut. It has a tough outer brown shell and edible white flesh inside. 3. Riddle (c): - Clue: 'I am a vegetable. I am pink in colour. I may also be white in colour. If you cut me, I make you cry. Who am I?' - Answer: Onion. Cutting an onion releases vapours that bring tears to our eyes. 4. Riddle (d): - Clue: 'I am a fruit. I come in green or purple. I come in a bunch. Who am I?' - Answer: Grapes. Grapes grow in clusters or bunches and are commonly green or purple.

q_and_a.question: Explain the central message and lessons taught in the poem 'I like food'.
q_and_a.answer: 1. Variety of Food: The poem tells us that there are lots of foods for us to taste, such as vegetables, fruits, and sweets. 2. Food as a Blessing: All foods and drinks with different flavours are special blessings from God. 3. Do Not Waste: Since food is a valuable blessing given by God, we should never waste it. We should eat up our food properly. 4. Gratitude: The poem teaches us to thank God for His favours and for providing yummy things that are nice for our small tummy.

q_and_a.question: Describe the scene in Picture 1 and Picture 2 where the children are sharing their food in the park.
q_and_a.answer: 1. In Picture 1, the teacher and pupils are in a nearby park. The teacher asks the pupils to share the food they brought from home. 2. The children open their lunchboxes and tell each other what they have brought: - One child brings poori with aloo dum. - Another child brings poori with dalma. - Other children bring fruits, cake, idli with chutney, aloo paratha, and chakuli. 3. In Picture 2, one girl says that her mother is sick, so she has no food. 4. Her caring friends immediately share their tiffin with her. One boy offers his paratha and another offers his chakuli. 5. The girl happily accepts their kind help and says, 'Thank you.'

q_and_a.question: Describe the syllable division exercise, rhyming words, and spelling practice presented in the chapter.
q_and_a.answer: 1. One-Syllable Words (Single Clap): - Words that have only one syllable sound: man, food, cat, hut, eat, mat, go, come, sit. - Students say each word aloud and clap once. 2. Two-Syllable Words (Two Claps): - Words broken into two distinct syllable sounds: - far - mer (farmer) - car - rot (carrot) - mar - ket (market) - brin - jal (brinjal) - man - go (mango) - break - fast (breakfast) - din - ner (dinner) - Students say each syllable and clap for every part. 3. Rhyming Pairs from the Poem 'I like food': - taste - waste - favours - flavours - food - should - yummy - tummy 4. Key Spelling Words: - Important chapter vocabulary words practiced by writing: blessing, tummy, sweets, hungry, gorilla.

q_and_a.question: Explain how farmers and animals help us get our daily food, and why we should be grateful to them.
q_and_a.answer: 1. Role of Farmers in Growing Crops: - Farmers work very hard in the fields under the sun and rain. - They cultivate and grow grains, cereals, vegetables, and fruits that we eat every day. 2. Contribution of Farm Animals and Insects: - Some farmers keep beehives with honey bees, from which we get sweet and healthy honey. - Some farmers keep cows. Cows provide us with fresh milk. - From cow's milk, we prepare many essential dairy products such as curds and butter. 3. Importance of Showing Gratitude: - Without farmers, we would not have meals to eat at home or school. - Therefore, we should always respect their hard work and say 'thank you' to our farmers. - In addition, we must show respect for their efforts by never wasting any food on our plates.

q_and_a.question: Read the story 'I like banana' and describe the conversation and events between the gorilla, the children, and Mummy.
q_and_a.answer: 1. A Big Visitor Arrives: - One day, a big gorilla comes to the house. - The gorilla greets the children and says that the food smells tasty and that he is hungry. 2. The Gorilla Asks for Food: - First, the gorilla politely asks, 'Can I have a banana please?' The children give it to him, and he eats all the bananas. - Next, he asks, 'Can I have a biscuit please?' The children hand over the biscuits, and the gorilla eats all of them. - Finally, the gorilla asks, 'Can I have an apple please?' The children give him apples, and he eats all the apples too. - After each item, the polite gorilla says, 'Thank you, mmm.' 3. Mummy Arrives Home: - After all the snacks are eaten, Mummy returns home. - Mummy greets everyone and asks in surprise, 'Where is all the food?' - The children reply that all the food is in the gorilla's tummy.

q_and_a.question: How many days are there in a week?
q_and_a.answer: There are seven days in a week.

q_and_a.question: How does the river flow in May, June, July, and August?
q_and_a.answer: The river runs very fast.

q_and_a.question: On which day is naughty Nandi ready for school?
q_and_a.answer: Nandi is ready for school on Sunday.

q_and_a.question: On which day does Nandi have a backache?
q_and_a.answer: Nandi has a backache on Saturday.

q_and_a.question: What happens to little naughty Nandi on Monday?
q_and_a.answer: Nandi has a fever on Monday.

q_and_a.question: What did Nanu Marandi do on Sunday?
q_and_a.answer: Nanu Marandi slept on Sunday.

q_and_a.question: What did Nanu Marandi do on Friday?
q_and_a.answer: Nanu Marandi clapped on Friday.

q_and_a.question: What is the name of the friend who was born on Monday?
q_and_a.answer: The friend's name is Nanu Marandi.

q_and_a.question: Which are the first and last months of the year?
q_and_a.answer: January is the first month of the year, and December is the last month.

q_and_a.question: Where does the river run in the last four months of the year?
q_and_a.answer: In September, October, November, and December, the river runs into the sea.

q_and_a.question: Where does the river run during the first four months of the year?
q_and_a.answer: In January, February, March, and April, the river runs down the hill.

q_and_a.question: How do we know that Nandi does not want to go to school?
q_and_a.answer: He pretends to be sick all through the school week from Monday to Saturday, but gets ready for school on Sunday when it is a holiday.

q_and_a.question: On which days does Nandi complain of a headache and a toothache?
q_and_a.answer: Nandi has a headache on Thursday and a toothache on Friday.

q_and_a.question: Which health problems does Nandi have on Tuesday and Wednesday?
q_and_a.answer: Nandi has a cold on Tuesday and a cough on Wednesday.

q_and_a.question: What did Nanu Marandi do on Wednesday and Thursday?
q_and_a.answer: Nanu Marandi jumped on Wednesday and played on Thursday.

q_and_a.question: Answer the following questions based on the chapter 'Days and Months': (a) Name all seven days of the week in correct order starting from Sunday. (b) Which day is usually a school holiday? (c) How do we know that little Nandi is not willing to go to school?
q_and_a.answer: (a) The seven days of the week in correct order are: 1. Sunday 2. Monday 3. Tuesday 4. Wednesday 5. Thursday 6. Friday 7. Saturday (b) Sunday is a school holiday. (c) We know that Nandi is not willing to go to school because he complains of different illnesses like fever, cold, cough, headache, toothache, and backache on all school days from Monday to Saturday, but gets ready for school on Sunday when the school is closed.

q_and_a.question: Based on the poem about the twelve months, describe the journey of the river across the different months of the year.
q_and_a.answer: The poem describes the journey of the river across twelve months divided into three groups: 1. January, February, March, and April: In these four months, the river runs down the hill. 2. May, June, July, and August: In these four months, the river runs very fast. 3. September, October, November, and December: In the last four months of the year, the river runs into the sea.

q_and_a.question: Describe what happens to little naughty Nandi from Monday to Sunday in the poem.
q_and_a.answer: In the poem 'Little Naughty Nandi', the child complains of different illnesses on different days of the week: 1. Monday: He has fever. 2. Tuesday: He has a cold. 3. Wednesday: He has a cough. 4. Thursday: He has a headache. 5. Friday: He has a toothache. 6. Saturday: He has a backache. 7. Sunday: He is ready to go to school. This shows that Nandi pretends to be sick during school days and gets ready for school only on Sunday, which is a holiday.

q_and_a.question: What actions did Nanu Marandi do on each day of the week according to the poem 'My friend Nanu Marandi'?
q_and_a.answer: According to the poem 'My friend Nanu Marandi', Nanu performed the following actions on each day of the week: 1. Monday: He was born. 2. Tuesday: He smiled. 3. Wednesday: He jumped. 4. Thursday: He played. 5. Friday: He clapped. 6. Saturday: He walked. 7. Sunday: He slept.

q_and_a.question: Based on the reading and activity sections of the chapter, answer the following questions: (a) From the given list of words: August, Thursday, September, March, Tuesday, Sunday, June, Saturday, Monday, May, January — separate them into days of the week and months of the year. (b) Identify the odd one out from each group and give a reason: Group 1: Thursday, Friday, August, Sunday Group 2: January, Tuesday, September, June (c) According to the colouring activity in the chapter, write the assigned colours for all seven days of the week.
q_and_a.answer: (a) Sorting the words: Days of the week: 1. Sunday 2. Monday 3. Tuesday 4. Thursday 5. Saturday Months of the year: 1. January 2. March 3. May 4. June 5. August 6. September (b) Odd one out: - Group 1 (Thursday, Friday, August, Sunday): The odd one is August because it is a month, while Thursday, Friday, and Sunday are days of the week. - Group 2 (January, Tuesday, September, June): The odd one is Tuesday because it is a day of the week, while January, September, and June are months of the year. (c) Assigned colours for the days of the week: 1. Monday: White 2. Tuesday: Red 3. Wednesday: Green 4. Thursday: Yellow 5. Friday: Pink 6. Saturday: Black 7. Sunday: Orange

q_and_a.question: Read the chapter 'Days and Months' carefully and answer the following questions in detail: (a) Write the names of all twelve months of the year in their proper order. (b) Which is the first month of the year? (c) Which is the last month of the year? (d) Write the month that comes before and after June. (e) Write the month that comes before and after November.
q_and_a.answer: (a) The twelve months of the year in correct order are: 1. January 2. February 3. March 4. April 5. May 6. June 7. July 8. August 9. September 10. October 11. November 12. December (b) The first month of the year is January. (c) The last month of the year is December. (d) For the month of June: - The month that comes before June is May. - The month that comes after June is July. (e) For the month of November: - The month that comes before November is October. - The month that comes after November is December.

q_and_a.question: What does Mummy tell Mohan to take before going to school?
q_and_a.answer: Mummy tells Mohan to take his umbrella before going to school.

q_and_a.question: What is our National Bird shown in the chapter?
q_and_a.answer: The peacock is our National Bird.

q_and_a.question: Where has Prithvi gone with his friends?
q_and_a.answer: Prithvi has gone to Shimla with his friends.

q_and_a.question: What is Dolly wearing in Hyderabad?
q_and_a.answer: Dolly is wearing a cotton frock.

q_and_a.question: Where are Dolly and her family visiting in summer?
q_and_a.answer: Dolly and her family are visiting Hyderabad, where her grandparents live.

q_and_a.question: What blooms every day during spring?
q_and_a.answer: Flowers bloom every day during spring.

q_and_a.question: Which season brings dew and chilly air?
q_and_a.answer: Pre-winter brings dew and chilly air.

q_and_a.question: What happens to the leaves during autumn?
q_and_a.answer: During autumn, the leaves begin to fall from the trees.

q_and_a.question: What does everyone want to do in summer to stay cool?
q_and_a.answer: To stay cool in summer, everyone wants to take a dip in the pool.

q_and_a.question: What are the six seasons mentioned in the chapter?
q_and_a.answer: The six seasons are summer, monsoon (rainy season), autumn, pre-winter (dewy season), winter, and spring.

q_and_a.question: According to the poem 'Rain', where does the rain fall?
q_and_a.answer: The rain falls on the green grass, on the trees, on the rooftops, and on the child.

q_and_a.question: What do Muni and Mohan need to protect themselves on a rainy day?
q_and_a.answer: Mohan needs an umbrella and Muni needs a raincoat to protect themselves from the rain.

q_and_a.question: How do people enjoy sunny days in winter?
q_and_a.answer: Winter is cold, so on sunny days people enjoy sitting outside in the warm sun rays.

q_and_a.question: What do people wear to warm their hands in pre-winter?
q_and_a.answer: People wear gloves to warm their hands because the air is chilly in pre-winter.

q_and_a.question: What do monsoon clouds bring, and how does the weather feel?
q_and_a.answer: Monsoon clouds are filled with rain. The rain makes the weather feel cool again.

q_and_a.question: Describe what Dolly, Prithvi, Mohan, and Muni do during their respective seasons as given in the chapter.
q_and_a.answer: The chapter describes the children in different seasons as follows: 1. Dolly in Summer: Dolly and her family visit Hyderabad where her grandparents live. Because it is hot there, she wears a light cotton frock. 2. Prithvi in Winter: Prithvi goes to Shimla with his friends. Because it is very cold and snowy, they wear warm woollen clothes like coats, caps, and gloves to play in the snow. 3. Mohan and Muni in the Rainy Season: Mohan and Muni are getting ready to go to school on a rainy day. Mohan takes his umbrella, and Muni asks for and wears her raincoat to protect herself from the rain.

q_and_a.question: What clothes do we wear during different seasons according to the chapter? Give examples for summer, winter, and the rainy season.
q_and_a.answer: According to the chapter, we wear different clothes to suit different seasons: 1. Summer: During summer, the weather is hot. We wear light and bright clothes made of cotton, such as cotton frocks and T-shirts, to keep ourselves cool. 2. Winter: During winter, the weather is cold and chilly. We wear warm woollen clothes such as sweaters, mufflers, woollen caps, and gloves to keep our bodies warm. 3. Rainy Season: In the rainy season, it rains frequently. We wear raincoats and carry umbrellas when going outside so that we do not get wet.

q_and_a.question: Name the six seasons described in the poem 'The Six Seasons' and write one line about each season as given in the chapter.
q_and_a.answer: The six seasons described in the poem are: 1. Summer: Summer is hot, and everyone wants a dip in the pool to stay cool. 2. Monsoon (Rainy Season): Monsoon clouds are filled with rain and make us feel cool again. 3. Autumn: Autumn is short, leaves begin to fall, and playing in the garden is fun. 4. Pre-winter (Dewy Season): Pre-winter brings dew and chilly air, and we wear gloves to warm our hands. 5. Winter: Winter is cold, and people enjoy the warm rays of the sun on sunny days. 6. Spring: Spring is a pleasant time when flowers bloom every day and children play happily.

q_and_a.question: Describe the features, weather, and activities of Summer, Rainy Season, and Winter based on what you have learned from the chapter.
q_and_a.answer: Based on the chapter, the three major seasons are described below: 1. Summer Season: - Weather: The summer season is very hot and sunny. The sun shines brightly in the sky. - Clothing: People wear light, bright, and white cotton clothes such as frocks and T-shirts. - Things we use and eat: People use ceiling fans, table fans, coolers, and air conditioners to stay cool. They like having cold drinks, lassi, and ice cream. - Activities: Children and people enjoy taking a dip in the pool or visiting the seabeach. 2. Rainy Season (Monsoon): - Weather: Monsoon clouds bring dark rain clouds and heavy showers. We hear thunder and see raindrops falling. - Clothing and Protection: People carry umbrellas and wear raincoats so that they do not get wet on the way to school or work. - Nature: Rain falls on the green grass, trees, and rooftops, making everything cool and fresh again. 3. Winter Season: - Weather: Winter is cold and chilly. Cold winds blow, and in hill stations like Shimla, snow falls. - Clothing: People wear woollen clothes like sweaters, jackets, mufflers, gloves, and warm caps. - Activities: People enjoy sitting near a fire or sitting outside to soak in the warm rays of the sun on sunny days. They also enjoy eating hot food and drinking warm drinks like soup.

q_and_a.question: Solve the following exercises from the chapter: (a) Unscramble the following letters to form names of seasons: i) n u m a u t ii) n r i p s g iii) m u s m r e iv) i w n e t r (b) State whether the following statements are 'Yes' (True) or 'No' (Not True): i) Dew falls on green grass in dewy season. ii) We wear cotton clothes in summer. iii) We use umbrellas in winter season. (c) Find the odd one out in each group and explain why: i) summer, winter, July, autumn ii) soup, ice-cream, cold drinks, lassi iii) muffler, sweater, gloves, raincoat
q_and_a.answer: (a) Unscrambled names of seasons: i) autumn ii) spring iii) summer iv) winter (b) 'Yes' or 'No' statements: i) Yes (Dew falls on green grass in dewy season). ii) Yes (We wear cotton clothes in summer to stay cool). iii) No (We do not use umbrellas in winter; umbrellas are used in the rainy season). (c) Odd one out: i) July (Summer, winter, and autumn are seasons, while July is the name of a month). ii) Soup (Ice-cream, cold drinks, and lassi are cold food items taken in summer, whereas soup is a hot item taken in winter). iii) Raincoat (Muffler, sweater, and gloves are warm woollen clothes worn in winter, while a raincoat is worn in the rainy season).

q_and_a.question: Read the following questions based on the chapter and answer each of them: (a) Write the names of the six seasons in their proper chronological order. (b) Which four seasons do we actually experience most noticeably? (c) What is pre-winter commonly known as? (d) Write the lines of the poem 'Rain'. (e) Write the lines of the poem 'Pitter Patter'.
q_and_a.answer: (a) The six seasons in proper order are: 1. Summer 2. Monsoon (Rainy season) 3. Autumn 4. Pre-winter 5. Winter 6. Spring (b) Although there are six seasons, we actually experience four main seasons: 1. Summer 2. Rainy season 3. Winter 4. Spring (c) Pre-winter is commonly known as the dewy season because dew falls on the green grass during this time. (d) The poem 'Rain': Rain on the green grass, Rain on the trees, Rain on the rooftops, And rain on me. (e) The poem 'Pitter Patter': I hear thunder, I hear thunder. Oh don't you? Pitter Patter rain drops. I am wet through.

q_and_a.question: ଓଡ଼ିଶାର ଏକ ଛୋଟ ନାମ ବିଶିଷ୍ଟ ସ୍ଥାନର ନାମ ଲେଖ ।
q_and_a.answer: ଓଡ଼ିଶାର ଏକ ଛୋଟ ନାମ ବିଶିଷ୍ଟ ସ୍ଥାନ ହେଉଛି ‘ଇବ୍’ ।

q_and_a.question: ଓଡ଼ିଶାର ପୁରୀ ଜିଲ୍ଲାରେ ଥିବା ଏକ ଲମ୍ବା ନାମ ବିଶିଷ୍ଟ ସ୍ଥାନର ନାମ କ’ଣ ?
q_and_a.answer: ପୁରୀ ଜିଲ୍ଲାରେ ଥିବା ଏହି ଲମ୍ବା ନାମ ବିଶିଷ୍ଟ ସ୍ଥାନଟି ହେଉଛି ‘ବୀର ପୁରୁଷୋତ୍ତମପୁର’ ।

q_and_a.question: ‘ସତର’ (୧୭) ସଂଖ୍ୟା ନାମରେ କେତୋଟି ଅକ୍ଷର ଅଛି ?
q_and_a.answer: ‘ସତର’ ସଂଖ୍ୟା ନାମରେ ୩ଟି ଅକ୍ଷର ଅଛି ।

q_and_a.question: ‘ତେଚାଳିଶ’ (୪୩) ସଂଖ୍ୟାର ନାମରେ କେତୋଟି ଅକ୍ଷର ରହିଛି ?
q_and_a.answer: ‘ତେଚାଳିଶ’ ସଂଖ୍ୟାର ନାମରେ ୪ଟି ଅକ୍ଷର ରହିଛି ।

q_and_a.question: ‘ମହାବଳ ବାଘ’ ନାମରେ କେତୋଟି ଅକ୍ଷର ଅଛି ?
q_and_a.answer: ‘ମହାବଳ ବାଘ’ ନାମରେ ୫ଟି ଅକ୍ଷର ଅଛି ।

q_and_a.question: ‘ସିଂହ’ ନାମରେ କେତୋଟି ଅକ୍ଷର ରହିଛି ?
q_and_a.answer: ‘ସିଂହ’ ନାମରେ ୨ଟି ଅକ୍ଷର ରହିଛି ।

q_and_a.question: ଦେବ ଓ ଦୀପାଙ୍କ ବନ୍ଧୁ ହେମନ୍ତ ପାଖରେ କେତୋଟି ଗାଈ ଓ କେତୋଟି ମେଣ୍ଢା ଥିଲେ ?
q_and_a.answer: ହେମନ୍ତ ପାଖରେ ୩୬ଟି ଗାଈ ଓ ୨୩ଟି ମେଣ୍ଢା ଥିଲେ ।

q_and_a.question: ଗାଈ ଚରାଇ ଫେରିବା ପରେ କାନ୍ଥରେ ଦୁଇଟି ଗାର ବଳକା ରହିବାର ଅର୍ଥ କ’ଣ ଥିଲା ?
q_and_a.answer: ଏହାର ଅର୍ଥ ଥିଲା ଯେ ଦୁଇଟି ଗାଈ ଘରକୁ ଫେରି ନାହାନ୍ତି ବା ହଜିଯାଇଛନ୍ତି ।

q_and_a.question: ସାଗର ଗାଁରେ ରହୁଥିବା ଦେବ ଓ ଦୀପାଙ୍କ ପରିବାରର ବୃତ୍ତି କ’ଣ ଥିଲା ?
q_and_a.answer: ଦେବ ଓ ଦୀପାଙ୍କ ପରିବାରର ବୃତ୍ତି ଗୋପାଳନ ଥିଲା ।

q_and_a.question: ବିଜୁଳି ଆବଶ୍ୟକ କରୁଥିବା ଏବଂ ବିଜୁଳି ଆବଶ୍ୟକ କରୁନଥିବା ଦୁଇଟି ଲେଖାଏଁ ଘରୋଇ ଜିନିଷର ନାମ ଲେଖ ।
q_and_a.answer: ବିଜୁଳି ଆବଶ୍ୟକ କରୁଥିବା ଦୁଇଟି ଜିନିଷ ହେଲା ଟିଭି ଓ ପଙ୍ଖା; ବିଜୁଳି ଆବଶ୍ୟକ କରୁନଥିବା ଦୁଇଟି ଜିନିଷ ହେଲା ଚୌକି ଓ ତକିଆ ।

q_and_a.question: ୨୧ ରୁ ୯୯ ଭିତରେ ଥିବା ଦୁଇଟି ଅକ୍ଷର ବିଶିଷ୍ଟ ସଂଖ୍ୟା ଦୁଇଟି କ’ଣ ଏବଂ ସେମାନଙ୍କ ମଧ୍ୟରୁ ସାନ କିଏ ?
q_and_a.answer: ସେହି ସଂଖ୍ୟା ଦୁଇଟି ହେଲା ‘ଅଶୀ’ (୮୦) ଓ ‘ନବେ’ (୯୦); ଏମାନଙ୍କ ମଧ୍ୟରୁ ‘ଅଶୀ’ ସାନ ଅଟେ ।

q_and_a.question: ୧ ରୁ ୯୯ ମଧ୍ୟରେ ୩ଟି ଅକ୍ଷର ଥିବା ଯେକୌଣସି ଦୁଇଟି ସଂଖ୍ୟାର ନାମ ଲେଖ ।
q_and_a.answer: ୩ଟି ଅକ୍ଷର ଥିବା ଦୁଇଟି ସଂଖ୍ୟାର ନାମ ହେଲା ‘ଏଗାର’ (୧୧) ଏବଂ ‘ଛପନ’ (୫୬) ।

q_and_a.question: ‘ମହେଶ’ ଏବଂ ‘ହୃସକେତନ’ ମଧ୍ୟରୁ କାହାର ନାମ ଲମ୍ବା ଏବଂ କାହିଁକି ?
q_and_a.answer: ‘ହୃସକେତନ’ ନାମଟି ଲମ୍ବା, କାରଣ ଏଥିରେ ୪ଟି ଅକ୍ଷର ଥିବା ବେଳେ ‘ମହେଶ’ ନାମରେ ମାତ୍ର ୩ଟି ଅକ୍ଷର ଅଛି ।

q_and_a.question: ପଶୁପକ୍ଷୀମାନଙ୍କ ଖେଳରେ ଦୁଇଟି ଦଳର ଦଳପତି କିପରି ବଛାଗଲା ?
q_and_a.answer: ଯାହାର ନାମ ସବୁଠାରୁ ଲମ୍ବା (ଅଧିକ ଅକ୍ଷର) ତାକୁ ପ୍ରଥମ ଦଳର ଏବଂ ଯାହାର ନାମ ସବୁଠାରୁ ଛୋଟ (କମ୍ ଅକ୍ଷର) ତାକୁ ଦ୍ୱିତୀୟ ଦଳର ଦଳପତି କରାଗଲା ।

q_and_a.question: ଗାଈମାନଙ୍କ ହିସାବ ରଖିବା ପାଇଁ ବନ୍ଧୁ ଦେବ ଓ ଦୀପାଙ୍କୁ କେଉଁ ଉପାୟ ବତାଇଥିଲେ ?
q_and_a.answer: ବାହାରକୁ ଯିବା ସମୟରେ ପ୍ରତ୍ୟେକ ଗାଈ ପାଇଁ କାନ୍ଥରେ ଗୋଟିଏ ଲେଖାଏଁ ଗାର ଟାଣିବା ଏବଂ ଫେରିବା ବେଳେ ଗୋଟିଏ ଗୋଟିଏ ଗାର ଲିଭାଇବା ପାଇଁ ବନ୍ଧୁ ଉପାୟ ବତାଇଥିଲେ ।

q_and_a.question: ସଂଖ୍ୟା କାର୍ଡ଼ ବ୍ୟବହାର କରି ଲୀନା ଓ ରାଜୁ କିପରି ସଂଖ୍ୟା ନାମ ଗଠନ କଲେ ? ‘ଛପନ’ ପରି ୩ଟି ଅକ୍ଷର ଥିବା ୧ ରୁ ୯୯ ମଧ୍ୟରେ ଥିବା ଅନ୍ୟ ପାଞ୍ଚୋଟି ସଂଖ୍ୟାର ନାମ ଉଦାହରଣ ସହ ଲେଖ ।
q_and_a.answer: ଲୀନା ଓ ରାଜୁ ସଂଖ୍ୟା କାର୍ଡ଼ ବ୍ୟବହାର କରି ସଂଖ୍ୟାର ନାମ ଏବଂ ସେଥିରେ ଥିବା ଅକ୍ଷର ସଂଖ୍ୟା ଗଣନା କରିଥିଲେ : - ଲୀନା ନିଜ ରୋଲ୍ ନମ୍ବର ୪୩ (ତେଚାଳିଶ) ତିଆରି କରିଥିଲା, ଯେଉଁଥିରେ ୪ଟି ଅକ୍ଷର ରହିଛି । - ରାଜୁ ନିଜ ରୋଲ୍ ନମ୍ବର ୧୭ (ସତର) ତିଆରି କରିଥିଲା, ଯେଉଁଥିରେ ୩ଟି ଅକ୍ଷର ରହିଛି । ‘ଛପନ’ (୫୬) ପରି ୩ଟି ଅକ୍ଷର ଥିବା ୧ ରୁ ୯୯ ମଧ୍ୟରେ ଅନ୍ୟ ପାଞ୍ଚୋଟି ସଂଖ୍ୟା ହେଲା : ୧. ଏଗାର (୧୧) – ଏ-ଗା-ର (୩ଟି ଅକ୍ଷର) ୨. ଚଉଦ (୧୪) – ଚ-ଉ-ଦ (୩ଟି ଅକ୍ଷର) ୩. ପନ୍ଦର (୧୫) – ପ-ନ୍ଦ-ର (୩ଟି ଅକ୍ଷର) ୪. ଷୋହଳ (୧୬) – ଷୋ-ହ-ଳ (୩ଟି ଅକ୍ଷର) ୫. ଅଠର (୧୮) – ଅ-ଠ-ର (୩ଟି ଅକ୍ଷର)

q_and_a.question: ଓଡ଼ିଶାର ସବୁଠାରୁ ଲମ୍ବା ନାମ ଥିବା ସ୍ଥାନ ଏବଂ ସବୁଠାରୁ ଛୋଟ ନାମ ଥିବା ସ୍ଥାନ ବିଷୟରେ ପାଠ ଆଧାରରେ ବର୍ଣ୍ଣନା କର ।
q_and_a.answer: ପାଠ୍ୟପୁସ୍ତକ ଅନୁଯାୟୀ ଓଡ଼ିଶାର ଦୁଇଟି ସ୍ଥାନର ନାମ ବିଷୟରେ ଆଲୋଚନା କରାଯାଇଛି : ୧. ଲମ୍ବା ନାମ ବିଶିଷ୍ଟ ସ୍ଥାନ : - ସ୍ଥାନର ନାମ : ‘ବୀର ପୁରୁଷୋତ୍ତମପୁର’ । - ଏହି ନାମଟି ବହୁତ ଲମ୍ବା ଏବଂ ଏଥିରେ ଅଧିକ ସଂଖ୍ୟକ ଅକ୍ଷର ରହିଛି । - ଏହି ସ୍ଥାନଟି ଓଡ଼ିଶାର ପୁରୀ ଜିଲ୍ଲାରେ ଅବସ୍ଥିତ । ୨. ଛୋଟ ନାମ ବିଶିଷ୍ଟ ସ୍ଥାନ : - ସ୍ଥାନର ନାମ : ‘ଇବ୍’ । - ଏହି ନାମଟି ଅତି ଛୋଟ ଏବଂ ଏଥିରେ କମ୍ ଅକ୍ଷର ରହିଛି । ଏହି ଉଦାହରଣ ମାଧ୍ୟମରେ ପିଲାମାନେ ଶବ୍ଦର ଲମ୍ବ ଏବଂ ଅକ୍ଷର ସଂଖ୍ୟା ବିଷୟରେ ସହଜରେ ଧାରଣା ପାଇପାରିବେ ।

q_and_a.question: ଦେବ ଓ ଦୀପା ଗାଈମାନଙ୍କର ହିସାବ କିପରି ରଖୁଥିଲେ ଏବଂ ଦିନେ କାନ୍ଥରେ ଦୁଇଟି ଗାର ବଳକା ରହିବାରୁ ସେମାନେ କ’ଣ କଲେ ?
q_and_a.answer: ଦେବ ଏବଂ ଦୀପାଙ୍କୁ ସଂଖ୍ୟା ଗଣିବା ଜଣା ନଥିଲା । ତେଣୁ ସେମାନଙ୍କ ବନ୍ଧୁ ତାଙ୍କୁ ଏକ ସହଜ ଉପାୟ ବତାଇଥିଲେ : ୧. ଗାଈମାନେ ଚରିବା ପାଇଁ ଫାଟକ ଦେଇ ବାହାରକୁ ଗଲାବେଳେ ପ୍ରତ୍ୟେକ ଗାଈ ପାଇଁ କାନ୍ଥରେ ଗୋଟିଏ ଲେଖାଏଁ ଗାର ଟଣାଯାଉଥିଲା । ୨. ସନ୍ଧ୍ୟାରେ ଗାଈମାନେ ଘରକୁ ଫେରି ଫାଟକ ଭିତରକୁ ପଶିବା ସମୟରେ ଗୋଟିଏ ଗୋଟିଏ ଗାରକୁ ଲିଭାଇ ଦିଆଯାଉଥିଲା । ୩. ଦିନେ ସବୁ ଗାଈ ଫେରିବା ପରେ ମଧ୍ୟ କାନ୍ଥରେ ଦୁଇଟି ଗାର ବଳକା ରହିଗଲା । ଏଥିରୁ ସେମାନେ ବୁଝିପାରିଲେ ଯେ ଦୁଇଟି ଗାଈ ହଜିଯାଇଛନ୍ତି ଏବଂ ଘରକୁ ଫେରିନାହାନ୍ତି । ୪. ଫଳରେ ଦେବ ଓ ଦୀପା ଚିନ୍ତିତ ହୋଇ ତୁରନ୍ତ ଖୋଜିବାକୁ ବାହାରିଲେ ଏବଂ ନିକଟସ୍ଥ ଏକ ପଡ଼ିଆରୁ ସେହି ଦୁଇଟି ଗାଈଙ୍କୁ ପାଇ ଖୁସିରେ ଘରକୁ ଫେରିଆସିଲେ ।

q_and_a.question: ହେମନ୍ତର ୩୬ଟି ଗାଈ ଏବଂ ୨୩ଟି ମେଣ୍ଢା ଥିଲେ । ଦେବ ଓ ଦୀପାଙ୍କ ପଦ୍ଧତି ଅନୁସାରେ ହେମନ୍ତ କିପରି ଗାର ଟାଣି ସେମାନଙ୍କର ହିସାବ ରଖିପାରିବ ଏବଂ ଏହି ପଦ୍ଧତିର ଉପଯୋଗିତା କ’ଣ ?
q_and_a.answer: ହେମନ୍ତ ପାଖରେ ଥିବା ଗୃହପାଳିତ ପଶୁମାନଙ୍କ ହିସାବ ରଖିବା ପାଇଁ ଦେବ ଏବଂ ଦୀପାଙ୍କ ଗାର ଟାଣିବା ପଦ୍ଧତି ଅତ୍ୟନ୍ତ ଉପଯୋଗୀ ଅଟେ । ୧. ଗାଈମାନଙ୍କ ପାଇଁ ଗାର ଟାଣିବା ପ୍ରଣାଳୀ : - ହେମନ୍ତ ପାଖରେ ମୋଟ ୩୬ଟି ଗାଈ ଅଛନ୍ତି । - ସେ ପ୍ରତି ୫ଟି ଗାଈ ପାଇଁ ଗୋଟିଏ ଗୋଷ୍ଠୀ କରି ୭ଟି ପୂର୍ଣ୍ଣ ଗୋଷ୍ଠୀ (୭ × ୫ = ୩୫) ଏବଂ ଅତିରିକ୍ତ ୧ଟି ଗାର ଟାଣିବ । ଅର୍ଥାତ୍ ମୋଟ ୩୬ଟି ଗାର କାନ୍ଥରେ ଟଣାଯିବ । ୨. ମେଣ୍ଢାମାନଙ୍କ ପାଇଁ ଗାର ଟାଣିବା ପ୍ରଣାଳୀ : - ହେମନ୍ତ ପାଖରେ ମୋଟ ୨୩ଟି ମେଣ୍ଢା ଅଛନ୍ତି । - ସେ ପ୍ରତି ୫ଟି ମେଣ୍ଢା ପାଇଁ ଗୋଟିଏ ଗୋଷ୍ଠୀ କରି ୪ଟି ପୂର୍ଣ୍ଣ ଗୋଷ୍ଠୀ (୪ × ୫ = ୨୦) ଏବଂ ଅତିରିକ୍ତ ୩ଟି ଗାର ଟାଣିବ । ଅର୍ଥାତ୍ ମୋଟ ୨୩ଟି ଗାର ଟଣାଯିବ । ୩. ଦୈନନ୍ଦିନ ହିସାବ ଓ ତଦାରଖ : - ସକାଳେ ଚରିବାକୁ ଯିବା ସମୟରେ ଫାଟକ ଦେଇ ବାହାରୁଥିବା ପ୍ରତ୍ୟେକ ପଶୁ ପାଇଁ ଗୋଟିଏ ଲେଖାଏଁ ଗାର ଟାଣିବ । - ସନ୍ଧ୍ୟାରେ ଫେରିବା ସମୟରେ ପ୍ରତ୍ୟେକ ପ୍ରବେଶ କରୁଥିବା ପଶୁ ପାଇଁ ଗୋଟିଏ ଲେଖାଏଁ ଗାର ଲିଭାଇ ଦେବ । ୪. ଏହି ପଦ୍ଧତିର ଉପଯୋଗିତା : - ସଂଖ୍ୟା ଗଣି ନଜାଣିଲେ ମଧ୍ୟ ସହଜରେ କୌଣସି ଜିନିଷ ବା ପଶୁ ହଜିଛି କି ନାହିଁ ଜାଣିହୁଏ । - ଯଦି ସନ୍ଧ୍ୟାରେ କୌଣସି ଗାର ବଳକା ରହିଯାଏ, ତେବେ ତୁରନ୍ତ ଜଣାପଡ଼ିବ ଯେ କେତୋଟି ପଶୁ ବାହାରେ ରହିଯାଇଛନ୍ତି ଏବଂ ସେମାନଙ୍କୁ ଖୋଜିବା ସହଜ ହେବ ।

q_and_a.question: ପାଠରେ ଥିବା ଆଠୋଟି ଘରୋଇ ବସ୍ତୁକୁ ଦୁଇଟି ଭିନ୍ନ ଉପାୟରେ ବର୍ଗୀକରଣ କରି ଦର୍ଶାଅ ।
q_and_a.answer: ପାଠରେ ଉଲ୍ଲେଖ ଥିବା ଆଠୋଟି ଘରୋଇ ବସ୍ତୁ ହେଲା : ଟିଭି, ଚୌକି, ଲ୍ୟାମ୍ପ, ପଲଙ୍କ, ଘଣ୍ଟି, ପଙ୍ଖା, ତକିଆ ଏବଂ କମ୍ବଳ । ପ୍ରଥମ ବର୍ଗୀକରଣ (ବିଜୁଳି ବ୍ୟବହାର ଆଧାରରେ) : ୧. ବିଜୁଳି ଆବଶ୍ୟକ କରୁଥିବା ବସ୍ତୁ : - ଟିଭି - ଲ୍ୟାମ୍ପ - ପଙ୍ଖା - ଘଣ୍ଟି ୨. ବିଜୁଳି ଆବଶ୍ୟକ କରୁନଥିବା ବସ୍ତୁ : - ଚୌକି - ପଲଙ୍କ - ତକିଆ - କମ୍ବଳ ଦ୍ୱିତୀୟ ବର୍ଗୀକରଣ (ବସ୍ତୁର ପ୍ରକୃତି ବା ନିର୍ମାଣ ସାମଗ୍ରୀ ଆଧାରରେ) : ୧. କାଠ ନିର୍ମିତ ଆସବାବପତ୍ର : - ଚୌକି - ପଲଙ୍କ ୨. ବିଛଣା ଓ କପଡ଼ା ଜାତୀୟ ସାମଗ୍ରୀ : - ତକିଆ - କମ୍ବଳ ଏହିପରି ଭାବରେ ବସ୍ତୁଗୁଡ଼ିକର ଗୁଣ ଓ ବ୍ୟବହାର ଅନୁସାରେ ସେଗୁଡ଼ିକୁ ଭିନ୍ନ ଭିନ୍ନ ଗୋଷ୍ଠୀରେ ବିଭକ୍ତ କରାଯାଇପାରେ ।

q_and_a.question: ପାଠରେ ଥିବା ପଶୁପକ୍ଷୀମାନଙ୍କ ନାମରେ କେତୋଟି ଲେଖାଏଁ ଅକ୍ଷର ଅଛି ତାଲିକା କର ଏବଂ ଦୁଇଟି ଦଳର ଦଳପତି କିପରି ବଛାଗଲା ବୁଝାଅ ।
q_and_a.answer: ଖେଳ ଖେଳିବା ପାଇଁ ପଶୁପକ୍ଷୀମାନଙ୍କ ମଧ୍ୟରୁ ଦୁଇଟି ଦଳ ଗଠନ କରାଯାଇଥିଲା । ନିୟମ ଅନୁସାରେ ଯାହାର ନାମ ସବୁଠାରୁ ଲମ୍ବା (ସବୁଠାରୁ ଅଧିକ ଅକ୍ଷର) ସେ ପ୍ରଥମ ଦଳର ଦଳପତି ଏବଂ ଯାହାର ନାମ ସବୁଠାରୁ ଛୋଟ (ସବୁଠାରୁ କମ୍ ଅକ୍ଷର) ସେ ଦ୍ୱିତୀୟ ଦଳର ଦଳପତି ହେବେ । ପଶୁପକ୍ଷୀଙ୍କ ନାମ ଏବଂ ଅକ୍ଷର ସଂଖ୍ୟାର ତାଲିକା : ୧. ମହାବଳ ବାଘ – ୫ଟି ଅକ୍ଷର ୨. କୁକୁର – ୩ଟି ଅକ୍ଷର ୩. ମୟୂର – ୩ଟି ଅକ୍ଷର ୪. ଡାମରା କାଉ – ୫ଟି ଅକ୍ଷର ୫. ସିଂହ – ୨ଟି ଅକ୍ଷର ୬. ଦନ୍ତାହାତୀ – ୪ଟି ଅକ୍ଷର ୭. ହରିଣ – ୩ଟି ଅକ୍ଷର ୮. ବଳଦ – ୩ଟି ଅକ୍ଷର ୯. ମାଛରଙ୍କା – ୪ଟି ଅକ୍ଷର ୧୦. ମାଙ୍କଡ଼ – ୩ଟି ଅକ୍ଷର ଦଳପତି ନିର୍ବାଚନ : - ପ୍ରଥମ ଦଳର ଦଳପତି : ‘ମହାବଳ ବାଘ’ କିମ୍ବା ‘ଡାମରା କାଉ’ (ଏମାନଙ୍କ ନାମରେ ସବୁଠାରୁ ଅଧିକ ୫ଟି ଅକ୍ଷର ଅଛି) । - ଦ୍ୱିତୀୟ ଦଳର ଦଳପତି : ‘ସିଂହ’ (ଏହାର ନାମରେ ସବୁଠାରୁ କମ୍ ୨ଟି ଅକ୍ଷର ଅଛି) ।

q_and_a.question: ଲୁଡୁ ଗୋଟିରେ ୨ ଟି ବିନ୍ଦୁ ଥିବା ପାର୍ଶ୍ୱର ବିପରୀତ ପାର୍ଶ୍ୱରେ କେତୋଟି ବିନ୍ଦୁ ଥାଏ ?
q_and_a.answer: ଲୁଡୁ ଗୋଟିରେ ୨ ଟି ବିନ୍ଦୁ ଥିବା ପାର୍ଶ୍ୱର ବିପରୀତ ପାର୍ଶ୍ୱରେ ୫ ଟି ବିନ୍ଦୁ ଥାଏ ।

q_and_a.question: ଲୁଡୁ ଗୋଟିର ୩ ଟି ବିନ୍ଦୁ ଥିବା ପାର୍ଶ୍ୱର ବିପରୀତ ପାର୍ଶ୍ୱରେ କେତୋଟି ବିନ୍ଦୁ ଥାଏ ?
q_and_a.answer: ଲୁଡୁ ଗୋଟିର ୩ ଟି ବିନ୍ଦୁ ଥିବା ପାର୍ଶ୍ୱର ବିପରୀତ ପାର୍ଶ୍ୱରେ ୪ ଟି ବିନ୍ଦୁ ଥାଏ ।

q_and_a.question: ଲୁଡୁ ଗୋଟିର ଆକୃତି କିପରି ଅଟେ ?
q_and_a.answer: ଲୁଡୁ ଗୋଟିର ଆକୃତି ସମଘନ ଅଟେ ।

q_and_a.question: ଆୟତଘନ ବାକ୍ସରେ ବିଲେଇର କେଉଁ ଅଂଶ ତିଆରି ହୋଇଥିଲା ?
q_and_a.answer: ଆୟତଘନ ବାକ୍ସରେ ବିଲେଇର ଲମ୍ବା ନିଶ ତିଆରି ହୋଇଥିଲା ।

q_and_a.question: କୋନ୍ ଆକୃତିର ଖେଳଣାରେ ପକ୍ଷୀର କେଉଁ ଅଂଶ ତିଆରି କରାଯାଇଥିଲା ?
q_and_a.answer: କୋନ୍ ଆକୃତିର ଖେଳଣାରେ ପକ୍ଷୀର ମୁନିଆ ଚଞ୍ଚୁ ତିଆରି କରାଯାଇଥିଲା ।

q_and_a.question: ପିଲାମାନେ ବୋତଲର ସିଲିଣ୍ଡର ଆକୃତିରେ କେଉଁ ପ୍ରାଣୀର ମୁହଁ ତିଆରି କରିଥିଲେ ?
q_and_a.answer: ପିଲାମାନେ ବୋତଲର ସିଲିଣ୍ଡର ଆକୃତିରେ କୁକୁର ଛୁଆର ମୁହଁ ତିଆରି କରିଥିଲେ ।

q_and_a.question: କେଉଁ ଆକୃତିର କୌଣସି ଧାର ନ ଥାଏ ?
q_and_a.answer: ଗୋଲକ ଆକୃତିର କୌଣସି ଧାର ନ ଥାଏ ।

q_and_a.question: ସମଘନ କେଉଁ ଆକୃତିର ଏକ ବିଶେଷ ପ୍ରକାର ଅଟେ ?
q_and_a.answer: ସମଘନ ଏକ ବିଶେଷ ପ୍ରକାରର ଆୟତଘନ ଅଟେ ।

q_and_a.question: ତିନୋଟି ସମଘନକୁ ପାଖାପାଖି ସିଧା ଧାଡ଼ିରେ ଯୋଡ଼ିଲେ କେଉଁ ଆକୃତି ତିଆରି ହେବ ?
q_and_a.answer: ତିନୋଟି ସମଘନକୁ ପାଖାପାଖି ସିଧା ଧାଡ଼ିରେ ଯୋଡ଼ିଲେ ଏକ ଆୟତଘନ ଆକୃତି ତିଆରି ହେବ ।

q_and_a.question: ଆମ ଚାରିପାଖରେ ଦେଖାଯାଉଥିବା କୋନ୍ ଏବଂ ସିଲିଣ୍ଡର ଆକୃତିର ଗୋଟିଏ ଲେଖାଏଁ ବସ୍ତୁର ନାମ ଲେଖ ।
q_and_a.answer: କୋନ୍ ଆକୃତିର ବସ୍ତୁ ହେଉଛି ଜନ୍ମଦିନ ଟୋପି ଏବଂ ସିଲିଣ୍ଡର ଆକୃତିର ବସ୍ତୁ ହେଉଛି ପାଣି ବୋତଲ ।

q_and_a.question: ଲୁଡୁ ଗୋଟିରେ ବିପରୀତ ପାର୍ଶ୍ୱରେ ଥିବା ବିନ୍ଦୁଗୁଡ଼ିକର ସଂରଚନାରେ କେଉଁ ନିୟମ ଦେଖାଯାଏ ?
q_and_a.answer: ଲୁଡୁ ଗୋଟିର ଯେକୌଣସି ପାର୍ଶ୍ୱ ଓ ତାର ବିପରୀତ ପାର୍ଶ୍ୱରେ ଥିବା ବିନ୍ଦୁଗୁଡ଼ିକର ଯୋଗଫଳ ସର୍ବଦା ୭ ହୋଇଥାଏ ।

q_and_a.question: ଘୁଷୁରିର ମୁହଁ ତିଆରି କରିବା ପାଇଁ କେଉଁ ଆକୃତିର ବାକ୍ସ ବ୍ୟବହାର କରାଯାଇଥିଲା ଏବଂ ଏହାର ଆଖି କିପରି ଥିଲା ?
q_and_a.answer: ଘୁଷୁରିର ମୁହଁ ତିଆରି କରିବା ପାଇଁ ସମଘନକାର ବାକ୍ସ ବ୍ୟବହାର କରାଯାଇଥିଲା ଏବଂ ଏହାର ଆଖି ଛୋଟ ଥିଲା ।

q_and_a.question: ଏକ ସମଘନ ଏବଂ ଏକ ଆୟତଘନକୁ ଏକାଠି ଯୋଡ଼ିଲେ କେଉଁ ଆକୃତି ମିଳେ ?
q_and_a.answer: ଏକ ସମଘନ ଏବଂ ଏକ ଆୟତଘନକୁ ଏକାଠି ଯୋଡ଼ିଲେ ଏକ ଆୟତଘନ ଆକୃତି ମିଳେ ।

q_and_a.question: ଉଭୟ ସିଧା ଏବଂ ବକ୍ର ପାର୍ଶ୍ୱ ଥିବା ଦୁଇଟି ଆକୃତିର ନାମ ଲେଖ ।
q_and_a.answer: ସିଲିଣ୍ଡର ଏବଂ କୋନ୍ ଆକୃତିର ଉଭୟ ସିଧା ଏବଂ ବକ୍ର ପାର୍ଶ୍ୱ ଥାଏ ।

q_and_a.question: କେଉଁ ଆକୃତିଗୁଡ଼ିକର କେବଳ ସିଧା ବା ସମତଳ ପାର୍ଶ୍ୱ ଥାଏ ? ଦୁଇଟି ଉଦାହରଣ ଦିଅ ।
q_and_a.answer: ସମଘନ ଏବଂ ଆୟତଘନ ଆକୃତିର କେବଳ ସିଧା ବା ସମତଳ ପାର୍ଶ୍ୱ ଥାଏ ।

q_and_a.question: ତିନୋଟି କିମ୍ବା ଛଅଟି ସମଘନକୁ (ଲୁଡୁ ଗୋଟି) ଯୋଡ଼ି କେଉଁ କେଉଁ ନୂଆ ଆକୃତି ତିଆରି କରାଯାଇପାରିବ ? ଉଦାହରଣ ସହ ବୁଝାଅ ।
q_and_a.answer: ସମଘନଗୁଡ଼ିକୁ ଏକାଠି ଯୋଡ଼ି ନିମ୍ନଲିଖିତ ନୂତନ ଆକୃତିଗୁଡ଼ିକ ତିଆରି କରାଯାଇପାରିବ: ୧. ଆୟତଘନ ନିର୍ମାଣ: • ତିନୋଟି କିମ୍ବା ଛଅଟି ସମଘନକୁ ଗୋଟିଏ ସିଧା ଧାଡ଼ିରେ ପାଖାପାଖି ଯୋଡ଼ି ରଖିଲେ ଏକ ଲମ୍ବା ଆୟତଘନ ଗଠିତ ହୁଏ । • ଛଅଟି ସମଘନକୁ ଦୁଇଟି ଧାଡ଼ିରେ ତିନି-ତିନି କରି ସଜାଇଲେ ମଧ୍ୟ ଏକ ଚଉଡ଼ା ଆୟତଘନ ପ୍ରସ୍ତୁତ ହୁଏ । ୨. ଟାୱାର (ସ୍ତମ୍ଭ) ନିର୍ମାଣ: • ସମଘନଗୁଡ଼ିକୁ ଗୋଟିକ ଉପରେ ଗୋଟିଏ ଉପରକୁ ଉପର ସଜାଇ ରଖିଲେ ଏକ ସୁନ୍ଦର ଟାୱାର ବା ଉଚ୍ଚ ସ୍ତମ୍ଭ ତିଆରି ହୁଏ । ୩. ପାହାଚ ଆକୃତି ନିର୍ମାଣ: • ସମଘନଗୁଡ଼ିକୁ ସ୍ତର ସ୍ତର କରି (ଯଥା: ତଳ ସ୍ତରରେ ତିନୋଟି, ମଝି ସ୍ତରରେ ଦୁଇଟି ଓ ଉପର ସ୍ତରରେ ଗୋଟିଏ) ସଜାଇ ପାହାଚ ଭଳି ନୂତନ ଆକୃତି ନିର୍ମାଣ କରାଯାଇପାରେ ।

q_and_a.question: ‘ସମଘନ ଏକ ବିଶେଷ ପ୍ରକାରର ଆୟତଘନ ଅଟେ’ - ଏହି ଉକ୍ତିଟିକୁ ବୁଝାଇ ସମଘନ ଏବଂ ଆୟତଘନ ମଧ୍ୟରେ ଥିବା ସମାନତା ଓ ପାର୍ଥକ୍ୟ ଲେଖ ।
q_and_a.answer: ସମଘନ ଏବଂ ଆୟତଘନର ଗଠନ ପ୍ରାୟ ସମାନ ଧରଣର ହୋଇଥିବାରୁ ସମଘନକୁ ଏକ ବିଶେଷ ପ୍ରକାରର ଆୟତଘନ କୁହାଯାଏ । ସମାନତା: ୧. ଉଭୟ ସମଘନ ଓ ଆୟତଘନର ସମସ୍ତ ପାର୍ଶ୍ୱ ସିଧା ଏବଂ ସମତଳ ଅଟେ । ୨. ଉଭୟଙ୍କର ଧାରଗୁଡ଼ିକ ସିଧା ଅଟେ । ୩. ଉଭୟଙ୍କର ପାର୍ଶ୍ୱ ଓ ଧାର ସଂଖ୍ୟା ସମାନ । ପାର୍ଥକ୍ୟ: ୧. ସମଘନର ପ୍ରତ୍ୟେକ ପାର୍ଶ୍ୱ ବର୍ଗାକାର ଏବଂ ସମସ୍ତ ପାର୍ଶ୍ୱ ପରସ୍ପର ସମାନ । ୨. ଆୟତଘନର ପାର୍ଶ୍ୱଗୁଡ଼ିକ ଆୟତାକାର ଏବଂ କେବଳ ବିପରୀତ ପାର୍ଶ୍ୱଗୁଡ଼ିକ ପରସ୍ପର ସମାନ ହୋଇଥାଏ ।

q_and_a.question: ଏକ ଲୁଡୁ ଗୋଟି କେଉଁ ଆକୃତିର ଅଟେ ? ଏହାର ବିଭିନ୍ନ ପାର୍ଶ୍ୱରେ ଥିବା ବିନ୍ଦୁ ଏବଂ ବିପରୀତ ପାର୍ଶ୍ୱଗୁଡ଼ିକ ମଧ୍ୟରେ ଥିବା ସମ୍ପର୍କ ବୁଝାଇ ଲେଖ ।
q_and_a.answer: ଲୁଡୁ ଗୋଟି ଏକ ସମଘନ ଆକୃତିର ବସ୍ତୁ ଅଟେ । ଏହାର ବିନ୍ଦୁ ଓ ପାର୍ଶ୍ୱଗୁଡ଼ିକର ସମ୍ପର୍କ: ୧. ଲୁଡୁ ଗୋଟିର ୬ ଗୋଟି ପାର୍ଶ୍ୱ ଥାଏ ଏବଂ ଏଥିରେ ୧ ରୁ ୬ ପର୍ଯ୍ୟନ୍ତ ବିନ୍ଦୁ ଚିହ୍ନିତ ଥାଏ । ୨. ଏହାର ବିପରୀତ ପାର୍ଶ୍ୱଗୁଡ଼ିକ ମଧ୍ୟରେ ଏକ ନିର୍ଦ୍ଦିଷ୍ଟ ନିୟମ ବା ସଂରଚନା ରହିଛି । ବିପରୀତ ପାର୍ଶ୍ୱରେ ଥିବା ବିନ୍ଦୁଗୁଡ଼ିକର ସମଷ୍ଟି ସର୍ବଦା ୭ ହୋଇଥାଏ । • ୧ ବିନ୍ଦୁ ଥିବା ପାର୍ଶ୍ୱର ବିପରୀତରେ ୬ ବିନ୍ଦୁ ଥାଏ (୧ + ୬ = ୭) । • ୨ ବିନ୍ଦୁ ଥିବା ପାର୍ଶ୍ୱର ବିପରୀତରେ ୫ ବିନ୍ଦୁ ଥାଏ (୨ + ୫ = ୭) । • ୩ ବିନ୍ଦୁ ଥିବା ପାର୍ଶ୍ୱର ବିପରୀତରେ ୪ ବିନ୍ଦୁ ଥାଏ (୩ + ୪ = ୭) ।

q_and_a.question: ନିମ୍ନଲିଖିତ ପ୍ରତ୍ୟେକ ଆକୃତିର ପାର୍ଶ୍ୱ ଏବଂ ଧାରର ବୈଶିଷ୍ଟ୍ୟଗୁଡ଼ିକ ଲେଖ: (କ) ଗୋଲକ (ଖ) ସମଘନ (ଗ) ସିଲିଣ୍ଡର (ଘ) କୋନ୍ ।
q_and_a.answer: ପ୍ରତ୍ୟେକ ଆକୃତିର ପାର୍ଶ୍ୱ ଏବଂ ଧାରର ବୈଶିଷ୍ଟ୍ୟ ନିମ୍ନରେ ପ୍ରଦାନ କରାଗଲା: (କ) ଗୋଲକ: • ଏହାର ପାର୍ଶ୍ୱ କେବଳ ବକ୍ର ଅଟେ । • ଏହାର କୌଣସି ସିଧା ଧାର ବା ଶୀର୍ଷ ନାହିଁ । (ଖ) ସମଘନ: • ଏହାର ସମସ୍ତ ପାର୍ଶ୍ୱ ସିଧା ଓ ସମତଳ ଅଟେ । • ଏହାର ସମସ୍ତ ଧାର ସିଧା ଅଟେ । (ଗ) ସିଲିଣ୍ଡର: • ଏହାର ଉଭୟ ସିଧା (ଉପର ଓ ତଳ ସମତଳ) ଏବଂ ବକ୍ର ପାର୍ଶ୍ୱ ରହିଛି । • ଏହାର ଧାରଗୁଡ଼ିକ ବକ୍ର ଅଟେ । (ଘ) କୋନ୍: • ଏହାର ଗୋଟିଏ ସମତଳ ପାର୍ଶ୍ୱ ଏବଂ ଗୋଟିଏ ବକ୍ର ପାର୍ଶ୍ୱ ରହିଛି । • ଏହାର ଗୋଟିଏ ବକ୍ର ଧାର ଏବଂ ଗୋଟିଏ ମୁନିଆ ଶୀର୍ଷ ଥାଏ ।

q_and_a.question: ବିଭିନ୍ନ ଜ୍ୟାମିତିକ ଆକୃତିକୁ (ସମଘନ, ଆୟତଘନ, ସିଲିଣ୍ଡର ଓ କୋନ୍) ଏକାଠି ବ୍ୟବହାର କରି ଏକ ଖେଳଣା ରକେଟ୍ ଏବଂ ଏକ ଖେଳଣା ଇଞ୍ଜିନ୍ କିପରି ସଜାଇ ତିଆରି କରାଯାଇପାରିବ, ତାହା ବର୍ଣ୍ଣନା କର ।
q_and_a.answer: ବିଭିନ୍ନ ଆକୃତି ବ୍ୟବହାର କରି ଖେଳଣା ସଜାଇବା ଏବଂ ନିର୍ମାଣ କରିବାର ପ୍ରଣାଳୀ ନିମ୍ନରେ ଦିଆଗଲା: ୧. ଖେଳଣା ରକେଟ୍ ନିର୍ମାଣ ପ୍ରଣାଳୀ: • ତଳ ଭାଗ (ଭିତ୍ତିଭୂମି): ସର୍ବପ୍ରଥମେ ତଳେ ଏକ ଆୟତଘନ କିମ୍ବା ସମଘନ ଆକୃତିର ବାକ୍ସ ରଖାଯାଏ, ଯାହା ରକେଟର ଆଧାର ଭାବେ କାମ କରେ । • ମଧ୍ୟ ଭାଗ (ମୁଖ୍ୟ ଶରୀର): ଆୟତଘନ ବାକ୍ସ ଉପରେ ଏକ ସିଲିଣ୍ଡର ଆକୃତିର ବୋତଲ ବା ଡବାକୁ ଲମ୍ବ ଭାବରେ ଠିଆ କରି ରଖାଯାଏ । • ଶୀର୍ଷ ଭାଗ (ଅଗ୍ରଭାଗ): ସିଲିଣ୍ଡରର ଉପରିଭାଗରେ ଏକ କୋନ୍ ଆକୃତିର ଖେଳଣା ରଖାଯାଏ, ଯାହାର ମୁନିଆ ଶୀର୍ଷ ରକେଟର ମୁହଁ ଭଳି ଦେଖାଯାଏ । • ଏହିପରି ଭାବରେ ଆୟତଘନ ଉପରେ ସିଲିଣ୍ଡର ଏବଂ ସିଲିଣ୍ଡର ଶୀର୍ଷରେ କୋନ୍ ସଜାଇ ରକେଟ୍ ତିଆରି ହୁଏ । ୨. ଖେଳଣା ଇଞ୍ଜିନ୍ ନିର୍ମାଣ ପ୍ରଣାଳୀ: • ତଳ ଭାଗ: ସର୍ବପ୍ରଥମେ ଏକ ବଡ଼ ଧୂସର ଆୟତଘନ ବାକ୍ସକୁ ଚେସିସ୍ ଭାବରେ ରଖାଯାଏ । • କ୍ୟାବିନ୍ ଅଂଶ: ଆୟତଘନର ଗୋଟିଏ ପାର୍ଶ୍ୱ ଉପରେ ନୀଳ ରଙ୍ଗର ସମଘନ ବାକ୍ସ ବସାଯାଏ । • ଇଞ୍ଜିନ୍ ବଡ଼ି: ଆୟତଘନର ଅନ୍ୟ ପାର୍ଶ୍ୱରେ ଲାଲ ରଙ୍ଗର ସିଲିଣ୍ଡର ଶୁଆଇ ରଖାଯାଏ । • ଚିମନି ବା ଉପର ଅଂଶ: ସିଲିଣ୍ଡର ଉପରେ ଏକ ଛୋଟ ହଳଦିଆ କୋନ୍ ଖଞ୍ଜାଯାଏ । • ଏହିପରି ବିଭିନ୍ନ ଆକୃତିଗୁଡ଼ିକୁ କ୍ରମରେ ସଜାଇ ଆକର୍ଷଣୀୟ ଖେଳଣା ଇଞ୍ଜିନ୍ ପ୍ରସ୍ତୁତ ହୁଏ ।

q_and_a.question: ଦୈନନ୍ଦିନ ଜୀବନରେ ବ୍ୟବହୃତ ବସ୍ତୁଗୁଡ଼ିକୁ ଆଧାର କରି ନିମ୍ନଲିଖିତ ଆକୃତିଗୁଡ଼ିକର ଦୁଇଟି ଲେଖାଏଁ ଉଦାହରଣ ଦିଅ ଏବଂ ସେଗୁଡ଼ିକର ପାର୍ଶ୍ୱ ଓ ଧାର ବିଷୟରେ ବିସ୍ତୃତ ଭାବରେ ବୁଝାଅ: (କ) ସମଘନ (ଖ) ଆୟତଘନ (ଗ) ସିଲିଣ୍ଡର (ଘ) କୋନ୍ (ଙ) ଗୋଲକ ।
q_and_a.answer: ବିଭିନ୍ନ ଆକୃତିର ବସ୍ତୁ ଓ ସେଗୁଡ଼ିକର ବିବରଣୀ ନିମ୍ନରେ ଦିଆଗଲା: (କ) ସମଘନ: • ଉଦାହରଣ: ଲୁଡୁ ଗୋଟି ଏବଂ ଚଉକା କାଠ ବାକ୍ସ । • ବିବରଣୀ: ଏହାର ସମସ୍ତ ପାର୍ଶ୍ୱ ସମାନ ବର୍ଗାକାର ଓ ସମତଳ । ଏହାର ପ୍ରତ୍ୟେକ ଧାର ସିଧା ଅଟେ । (ଖ) ଆୟତଘନ: • ଉଦାହରଣ: ଇଟା ଏବଂ ଦିଆସିଲି ଖୋଳ । • ବିବରଣୀ: ଏହାର ପାର୍ଶ୍ୱଗୁଡ଼ିକ ଆୟତାକାର ଓ ସମତଳ । ଏହାର ସମସ୍ତ ଧାର ସିଧା ହୋଇଥାଏ ଏବଂ ବିପରୀତ ପାର୍ଶ୍ୱଗୁଡ଼ିକ ପରସ୍ପର ସମାନ । (ଗ) ସିଲିଣ୍ଡର: • ଉଦାହରଣ: ପାଣି ବୋତଲ ଏବଂ ଟିଣ ଡବା । • ବିବରଣୀ: ଏହାର ଉପର ଓ ତଳ ଭାଗ ସମତଳ (ଗୋଲାକାର) ଏବଂ ମଝି ଅଂଶଟି ବକ୍ର ପାର୍ଶ୍ୱ ଅଟେ । ଏହାର ଧାରଗୁଡ଼ିକ ବକ୍ର ଅଟେ । (ଘ) କୋନ୍: • ଉଦାହରଣ: ଜନ୍ମଦିନ ଟୋପି ଏବଂ ଆଇସକ୍ରିମ୍ କୋନ୍ । • ବିବରଣୀ: ଏହାର ତଳ ପାର୍ଶ୍ୱଟି ସମତଳ ଓ ଗୋଲାକାର ଏବଂ ଉପର ଅଂଶଟି ବକ୍ର ପାର୍ଶ୍ୱ ଅଟେ । ଏହାର ଗୋଟିଏ ବକ୍ର ଧାର ଓ ଗୋଟିଏ ମୁନିଆ ଶୀର୍ଷ ଥାଏ । (ଙ) ଗୋଲକ: • ଉଦାହରଣ: ଖେଳ ଫୁଟବଲ ଏବଂ ଗ୍ଲୋବ୍ । • ବିବରଣୀ: ଏହାର କେବଳ ଗୋଟିଏ ବକ୍ର ପାର୍ଶ୍ୱ ଥାଏ । ଏହାର କୌଣସି ଧାର ବା ଶୀର୍ଷ ନଥାଏ ।

q_and_a.question: କ୍ରିକେଟ ଖେଳରେ ଜଣେ ଖେଳାଳି ‘ଶତକ’ ହାସଲ କଲେ କେତେ ରନ୍ ବୁଝାଏ ?
q_and_a.answer: କ୍ରିକେଟ ଖେଳରେ ‘ଶତକ’ ହାସଲ କଲେ ୧୦୦ ରନ୍ ବୁଝାଏ ।

q_and_a.question: ୧ଟି ଶହେ ବିଡ଼ା, ୫ଟି ଦଶ ବିଡ଼ା ଏବଂ ୭ଟି ଖୋଲା କାଠି ମିଶିଲେ କେଉଁ ସଂଖ୍ୟା ହେବ ?
q_and_a.answer: ୧ଟି ଶହେ ବିଡ଼ା, ୫ଟି ଦଶ ବିଡ଼ା ଏବଂ ୭ଟି ଖୋଲା କାଠି ମିଶିଲେ ସଂଖ୍ୟାଟି ୧୫୭ (ଏକଶହ ସତାବନ) ହେବ ।

q_and_a.question: ୧୨୦ ସଂଖ୍ୟାର ୧ କମ୍ ଏବଂ ୧ ଅଧିକ ସଂଖ୍ୟା କେତେ ?
q_and_a.answer: ୧୨୦ ସଂଖ୍ୟାର ୧ କମ୍ ସଂଖ୍ୟା ୧୧୯ ଏବଂ ୧ ଅଧିକ ସଂଖ୍ୟା ୧୨୧ ଅଟେ ।

q_and_a.question: ୬୦ ସହିତ କେତେ ମିଶାଇଲେ ୧୦୦ ହୁଏ ?
q_and_a.answer: ୬୦ ସହିତ ୪୦ ମିଶାଇଲେ ୧୦୦ ହୁଏ ।

q_and_a.question: ୯୯ ସଂଖ୍ୟାର ପରବର୍ତ୍ତୀ ସଂଖ୍ୟା କେତେ ?
q_and_a.answer: ୯୯ ସଂଖ୍ୟାର ପରବର୍ତ୍ତୀ ସଂଖ୍ୟା ହେଉଛି ୧୦୦ (ଏକଶହ) ।

q_and_a.question: ଶୂନ (୦) ସଂକେତର ପ୍ରକୃତ ଅର୍ଥ କ'ଣ ?
q_and_a.answer: ଶୂନ (୦) ସଂକେତର ପ୍ରକୃତ ଅର୍ଥ ହେଉଛି “କିଛି ନୁହେଁ” ।

q_and_a.question: ପ୍ରାଚୀନ ଭାରତୀୟମାନେ ସଂଖ୍ୟା ଲେଖିବା ପାଇଁ କେତୋଟି ସଂକେତ ତିଆରି କରିଥିଲେ ଓ ସେଗୁଡ଼ିକ କ'ଣ କ'ଣ ?
q_and_a.answer: ପ୍ରାଚୀନ ଭାରତୀୟମାନେ ମାତ୍ର ୧୦ଟି ସଂକେତ ତିଆରି କରିଥିଲେ । ସେଗୁଡ଼ିକ ହେଲା ୦, ୧, ୨, ୩, ୪, ୫, ୬, ୭, ୮ ଓ ୯ ।

q_and_a.question: ପ୍ରାଚୀନ କାଳରେ ଲୋକମାନେ ହିସାବ ରଖିବା ପାଇଁ କେଉଁଠାରେ ଚିହ୍ନ କରୁଥିଲେ ?
q_and_a.answer: ପ୍ରାଚୀନ କାଳରେ ଲୋକମାନେ ନିଜ ଜିନିଷର ହିସାବ ରଖିବା ପାଇଁ ଗୁମ୍ଫାର କାନ୍ଥ ଓ ଗଛର ଛାଲିରେ ଚିହ୍ନ କରୁଥିଲେ ।

q_and_a.question: ୧୮୨ ସଂଖ୍ୟାର ପୂର୍ବବର୍ତ୍ତୀ ଏବଂ ପରବର୍ତ୍ତୀ ସଂଖ୍ୟା ଦୁଇଟି ଲେଖ ।
q_and_a.answer: ୧୮୨ ସଂଖ୍ୟାର ପୂର୍ବବର୍ତ୍ତୀ ସଂଖ୍ୟା ହେଉଛି ୧୮୧ ଏବଂ ପରବର୍ତ୍ତୀ ସଂଖ୍ୟା ହେଉଛି ୧୮୩ ।

q_and_a.question: ସଂଖ୍ୟା ରେଖାରେ ୨୦୦ ପୂରଣ କରିବା ପାଇଁ ୧୫୦ ଏବଂ ୧୩୦ ସହିତ କେତେ ଯୋଗ କରିବାକୁ ପଡ଼ିବ ?
ବେଙ୍ଗଟି ୧୦୦ରୁ ଆରମ୍ଭ କରି ପ୍ରତି ଥର ୨୦ ଡେଇଁଲେ, ପରବର୍ତ୍ତୀ ତିନୋଟି ଡିଆଁରେ କେଉଁ କେଉଁ ସଂଖ୍ୟାରେ ପହଞ୍ଚିବ ?
q_and_a.answer: ବେଙ୍ଗଟି ପରବର୍ତ୍ତୀ ତିନୋଟି ଡିଆଁରେ ଯଥାକ୍ରମେ ୧୨୦, ୧୪୦ ଏବଂ ୧୬୦ ସଂଖ୍ୟାରେ ପହଞ୍ଚିବ ।

q_and_a.question: ୧୨୩ ସଂଖ୍ୟାଟିରେ କେତୋଟି ଶହେ ବିଡ଼ା, କେତୋଟି ଦଶ ବିଡ଼ା ଓ କେତୋଟି ଖୋଲା କାଠି ଥାଏ ?
q_and_a.answer: ୧୨୩ ସଂଖ୍ୟାରେ ୧ଟି ଶହେ (୧୦୦)ର ବିଡ଼ା, ୨ଟି ଦଶ (୧୦)ର ବିଡ଼ା ଏବଂ ୩ଟି ଖୋଲା କାଠି ଥାଏ ।

q_and_a.question: ତାଳି - ତୁଟକି ତୁଟକି - ଥାପ୍ ଥାପ୍ ଥାପ୍ କହିଲେ କେଉଁ ସଂଖ୍ୟାକୁ ବୁଝାଇବ ?
q_and_a.answer: ୧ଟି ତାଳି (୧୦୦), ୨ଟି ତୁଟକି (୨୦) ଏବଂ ୩ଟି ଥାପ୍ (୩) ମିଶି ସଂଖ୍ୟା ୧୨୩ (ଏକଶହ ତେଇଶି)କୁ ବୁଝାଇବ ।

q_and_a.question: ‘ତାଳି, ତୁଟକି ଏବଂ ଥାପ୍’ ଖେଳରେ ଗୋଟିଏ ତାଳି, ଗୋଟିଏ ତୁଟକି ଓ ଗୋଟିଏ ଥାପ୍ କେଉଁ କେଉଁ ସଂଖ୍ୟାକୁ ବୁଝାଏ ?
q_and_a.answer: ଏହି ଖେଳରେ ଗୋଟିଏ ତାଳି ୧୦୦କୁ, ଗୋଟିଏ ତୁଟକି ୧୦କୁ ଏବଂ ଗୋଟିଏ ଥାପ୍ ୧କୁ ବୁଝାଏ ।

q_and_a.question: ୧୦୦ଟି ଦିଆସିଲି କାଠି ପାଇଁ ୧୦ ଟିକିଆ କେତୋଟି ବିଡ଼ା ଆବଶ୍ୟକ ହୁଏ ?
q_and_a.answer: ୧୦୦ଟି ଦିଆସିଲି କାଠି ପାଇବା ପାଇଁ ୧୦ ଟିକିଆ କାଠିର ୧୦ଟି ବିଡ଼ା ଆବଶ୍ୟକ ହୁଏ ।

q_and_a.question: 'ତାଳି, ତୁଟକି ଏବଂ ଥାପ୍' ଖେଳର ନିୟମ ବୁଝାଅ । ଏହି ନିୟମ ଅନୁସାରେ (କ) ୧୩୫ ଏବଂ (ଖ) ୨୧୨ କୁ କିପରି ସୂଚିତ କରାଯିବ ଲେଖ ।
q_and_a.answer: 'ତାଳି, ତୁଟକି ଏବଂ ଥାପ୍' ଖେଳର ନିୟମ ଓ ସଂଖ୍ୟା ପ୍ରଦର୍ଶନ ପ୍ରଣାଳୀ : ୧. ଖେଳର ମୂଳ ନିୟମ : - ଗୋଟିଏ ତାଳି = ୧୦୦ (ଶହେ) କୁ ବୁଝାଏ । ଦୁଇଟି ତାଳି = ୨୦୦ କୁ ବୁଝାଏ । - ଗୋଟିଏ ତୁଟକି = ୧୦ (ଦଶ) କୁ ବୁଝାଏ । ଦୁଇଟି ତୁଟକି = ୨୦ କୁ ବୁଝାଏ । - ଗୋଟିଏ ଥାପ୍ = ୧ (ଏକ) କୁ ବୁଝାଏ । ଦୁଇଟି ଥାପ୍ = ୨ କୁ ବୁଝାଏ । ୨. ପ୍ରଦତ୍ତ ସଂଖ୍ୟାର ସୂଚନା : (କ) ୧୩୫ (ଏକଶହ ପଞ୍ଚତିରିଶି) : - ଏଥିରେ ୧ଟି ଶହେ, ୩ଟି ଦଶ ଏବଂ ୫ଟି ଏକ ଅଛି । - ଏଣୁ ଏହାକୁ ପ୍ରକାଶ କରିବା ପାଇଁ : ୧ ତାଳି - ୩ ତୁଟକି - ୫ ଥାପ୍ ମରାଯିବ । (ଖ) ୨୧୨ (ଦୁଇଶହ ବାର) : - ଏଥିରେ ୨ଟି ଶହେ, ୧ଟି ଦଶ ଏବଂ ୨ଟି ଏକ ଅଛି । - ଏଣୁ ଏହାକୁ ପ୍ରକାଶ କରିବା ପାଇଁ : ୨ ତାଳି - ୧ ତୁଟକି - ୨ ଥାପ୍ ମରାଯିବ ।

q_and_a.question: '୧୦୦' ବା ଶତକ କହିଲେ କ'ଣ ବୁଝ ? ବିଭିନ୍ନ ଉପାୟରେ ୧୦୦ ଗଠନ କରିବାର ଚାରୋଟି ଉଦାହରଣ ଦିଅ ।
ପ୍ରାଚୀନ କାଳରେ ଲୋକମାନେ କିପରି ଗଣନା କରୁଥିଲେ ଏବଂ ପ୍ରାଚୀନ ଭାରତୀୟମାନଙ୍କ ସଂଖ୍ୟା ଲେଖିବା ପଦ୍ଧତି କାହିଁକି ଏକ ଶ୍ରେଷ୍ଠ ଆବିଷ୍କାର ଥିଲା ? ବୁଝାଇ ଲେଖ ।
q_and_a.answer: ପ୍ରାଚୀନ କାଳର ଗଣନା ପ୍ରଣାଳୀ ଏବଂ ଭାରତୀୟ ପଦ୍ଧତିର ବିବରଣୀ ନିମ୍ନରେ ଦିଆଗଲା : ୧. ପ୍ରାଚୀନ କାଳର ଗଣନା : ହଜାର ହଜାର ବର୍ଷ ପୂର୍ବେ ଲୋକମାନେ ନିଜ ଜିନିଷର ହିସାବ ରଖିବା ପାଇଁ ଗୁମ୍ଫାର କାନ୍ଥ ଓ ଗଛର ଛାଲିରେ ବିଭିନ୍ନ ଚିହ୍ନ କରୁଥିଲେ । ସମୟ କ୍ରମେ ସେମାନେ ୫, ୧୦, ୨୦ ଓ ୬୦ ଟିକିଆ ଦଳ ତିଆରି କରି ହିସାବ ରଖିବା ଶିଖିଲେ । ୨. ଭାରତୀୟମାନଙ୍କ ଆବିଷ୍କାର : ପ୍ରାଚୀନ ଭାରତୀୟମାନେ ମାତ୍ର ୧୦ଟି ସଂକେତ (୦, ୧, ୨, ୩, ୪, ୫, ୬, ୭, ୮, ୯) ବ୍ୟବହାର କରି ଯେକୌଣସି ସଂଖ୍ୟା ଲେଖିବାର ଏକ ସ୍ଵଦେଶୀ ପଦ୍ଧତି ତିଆରି କରିଥିଲେ । ୩. ଶୂନ (୦)ର ଗୁରୁତ୍ଵ : ଏହି ପଦ୍ଧତିରେ ଶୂନ (୦) ସଂକେତର ବ୍ୟବହାର ସବୁଠାରୁ ଗୁରୁତ୍ଵପୂର୍ଣ୍ଣ ଥିଲା, ଯାହାର ଅର୍ଥ 'କିଛି ନୁହେଁ' । ଏହି '୦' ଯୋଗୁଁ ହିଁ ସଂଖ୍ୟା ଲେଖିବାର ପ୍ରଣାଳୀ ସହଜ ଓ ସମ୍ଭବପର ହୋଇପାରିଲା । ୪. ଆଧୁନିକ ଯୁଗରେ ପ୍ରଭାବ : ଏହି ସଂଖ୍ୟା ପଦ୍ଧତି ଆଧାରରେ ହିଁ ଆଜିର ଟିଭି, କମ୍ପ୍ୟୁଟର, ମୋବାଇଲ୍ ଫୋନ୍ ଆଦି ବୈଷୟିକ ଜ୍ଞାନକୌଶଳର ବିକାଶ ସମ୍ଭବ ହୋଇଛି ଏବଂ ଏହା ସମଗ୍ର ବିଶ୍ଵରେ ବ୍ୟବହୃତ ହେଉଛି ।

q_and_a.question: ସଂଖ୍ୟାର '୧ କମ୍' (ପୂର୍ବବର୍ତ୍ତୀ) ଏବଂ '୧ ଅଧିକ' (ପରବର୍ତ୍ତୀ) ସଂଖ୍ୟା କହିଲେ କ'ଣ ବୁଝ ? ନିମ୍ନଲିଖିତ ସଂଖ୍ୟାଗୁଡ଼ିକର ସାରଣୀ ପୂରଣ କରି ବୁଝାଅ : ୧୨୦, ୧୨୯, ୧୩୪, ୧୪୮, ୧୮୨ । ଏହା ସହିତ ପାଠରେ ଥିବା 'କଥାକୁହା ପାତ୍ର'ର ନିୟମ ଉଦାହରଣ ସହ ଲେଖ ।
q_and_a.answer: ସଂଖ୍ୟାର ପୂର୍ବବର୍ତ୍ତୀ ଓ ପରବର୍ତ୍ତୀ ସଂଖ୍ୟାର ଧାରଣା ଏବଂ କଥାକୁହା ପାତ୍ରର ନିୟମ ନିମ୍ନରେ ପ୍ରଦତ୍ତ ହେଲା : ୧. ଧାରଣା : - '୧ କମ୍' (ପୂର୍ବବର୍ତ୍ତୀ ସଂଖ୍ୟା) : ଯେକୌଣସି ସଂଖ୍ୟାରୁ ୧ ବିୟୋଗ କଲେ ତାହାର ଠିକ୍ ପୂର୍ବ ସଂଖ୍ୟା ମିଳେ । - '୧ ଅଧିକ' (ପରବର୍ତ୍ତୀ ସଂଖ୍ୟା) : ଯେକୌଣସି ସଂଖ୍ୟାରେ ୧ ଯୋଗ କଲେ ତାହାର ଠିକ୍ ପର ସଂଖ୍ୟା ମିଳେ । ୨. ସାରଣୀ ପୂରଣ : - ସଂଖ୍ୟା ୧୨୦ : ୧ କମ୍ = ୧୧୯ | ସଂଖ୍ୟା = ୧୨୦ | ୧ ଅଧିକ = ୧୨୧ - ସଂଖ୍ୟା ୧୨୯ : ୧ କମ୍ = ୧୨୮ | ସଂଖ୍ୟା = ୧୨୯ | ୧ ଅଧିକ = ୧୩୦ - ସଂଖ୍ୟା ୧୩୪ : ୧ କମ୍ = ୧୩୩ | ସଂଖ୍ୟା = ୧୩୪ | ୧ ଅଧିକ = ୧୩୫ - ସଂଖ୍ୟା ୧୪୮ : ୧ କମ୍ = ୧୪୭ | ସଂଖ୍ୟା = ୧୪୮ | ୧ ଅଧିକ = ୧୪୯ - ସଂଖ୍ୟା ୧୮୨ : ୧ କମ୍ = ୧୮୧ | ସଂଖ୍ୟା = ୧୮୨ | ୧ ଅଧିକ = ୧୮୩ ୩. 'କଥାକୁହା ପାତ୍ର'ର ଖେଳ ଓ ନିୟମ : - ନିୟମ : କଥାକୁହା ପାତ୍ରକୁ ଯେକୌଣସି ସଂଖ୍ୟା କହିଲେ, ସେ ତାହାର ଠିକ୍ ପରବର୍ତ୍ତୀ ସଂଖ୍ୟା (୧ ଅଧିକ) କହିଥାଏ । - ଉଦାହରଣ : * ଆମେ କହିଲେ ୪୨, ପାତ୍ର କହିବ ୪୩ * ଆମେ କହିଲେ ୯୯, ପାତ୍ର କହିବ ୧୦୦ * ଆମେ କହିଲେ ୧୦୯, ପାତ୍ର କହିବ ୧୧୦ * ଆମେ କହିଲେ ୧୨୭, ପାତ୍ର କହିବ ୧୨୮ * ପାତ୍ର ଯଦି ୧୫୦ କହେ, ତେବେ ଆମେ ୧୪୯ କହିଥିଲେ ।

q_and_a.question: 'ଦ୍ବିଶତକ' ବା '୨୦୦' ସଂଖ୍ୟାର ବିଭିନ୍ନ ଗଠନ ପ୍ରଣାଳୀ ଲେଖ ଏବଂ ସଂଖ୍ୟା ରେଖାରେ ବେଙ୍ଗଡିଆଁ ଖେଳ ମାଧ୍ୟମରେ (କ) ୫ ଲେଖାଏଁ ଏବଂ (ଖ) ୨୦ ଲେଖାଏଁ ଡେଇଁ ଖାଲିସ୍ଥାନ ପୂରଣ କରିବା ପଦ୍ଧତି ବୁଝାଅ ।
q_and_a.answer: 'ଦ୍ବିଶତକ'ର ଧାରଣା ଏବଂ ସଂଖ୍ୟା ରେଖାରେ ବେଙ୍ଗଡିଆଁ ଖେଳର ବିସ୍ତୃତ ବିବରଣୀ : ୧. ଦ୍ବିଶତକ (୨୦୦)ର ଧାରଣା : - 'ଦ୍ବିଶତକ' ଅର୍ଥ ଦୁଇଟି ଶହ ବା ୨୦୦ । - ୧୦୦ଟି କାଠି ଥିବା ୨ଟି ବଡ଼ ବିଡ଼ା ଏକାଠି ହେଲେ ୨୦୦ ହୁଏ । - ବିଭିନ୍ନ ଯୋଗଫଳ ରୂପେ ପ୍ରକାଶ : * ୧୫୦ + ୫୦ = ୨୦୦ * ୧୩୦ + ୭୦ = ୨୦୦ * ୧୦୦ + ୧୦୦ = ୨୦୦ ୨. ସଂଖ୍ୟା ରେଖାରେ ବେଙ୍ଗଡିଆଁ ଖେଳ : (କ) ୫ ଲେଖାଏଁ ଡେଇଁବା (୧୦୦ ରୁ ୧୫୦ ପର୍ଯ୍ୟନ୍ତ) : ବେଙ୍ଗଟି ପ୍ରତି ଥର ୫ ଘର ଆଗକୁ ଡିଏଁ । ଏହାର କ୍ରମ ହେବ : ୧୦୦ — ୧୦୫ — ୧୧୦ — ୧୧୫ — ୧୨୦ — ୧୨୫ — ୧୩୦ — ୧୩୫ — ୧୪୦ — ୧୪୫ — ୧୫୦ । ଏଠାରେ ପ୍ରତ୍ୟେକ ସଂଖ୍ୟାରେ ୫ ଯୋଗ ହୋଇ ପରବର୍ତ୍ତୀ ସଂଖ୍ୟା ମିଳେ । (ଖ) ୨୦ ଲେଖାଏଁ ଡେଇଁବା (୧୦୦ ରୁ ୨୦୦ ପର୍ଯ୍ୟନ୍ତ) : ବେଙ୍ଗଟି ପ୍ରତି ଥର ୨୦ ଘର ଆଗକୁ ଡିଏଁ । ଏହାର କ୍ରମ ହେବ : ୧୦୦ — ୧୨୦ — ୧୪୦ — ୧୬୦ — ୧୮୦ — ୨୦୦ । ଏଠାରେ ପ୍ରତ୍ୟେକ ସଂଖ୍ୟାରେ ୨୦ ଯୋଗ ହୋଇ ଶେଷରେ ୨୦୦ (ଦ୍ବିଶତକ) ରେ ପହଞ୍ଚାଯାଏ ।

q_and_a.question: ଦିଆସିଲି କାଠିର ବିଡ଼ା (୧୦୦ର ବିଡ଼ା, ୧୦ର ବିଡ଼ା) ଏବଂ ଖୋଲା କାଠି ବ୍ୟବହାର କରି ନିମ୍ନଲିଖିତ ସଂଖ୍ୟାଗୁଡ଼ିକୁ କିପରି ସଜାଇ ଲେଖାଯିବ, ସାରଣୀ ସହ ବୁଝାଇ ଲେଖ : (କ) ୧୨୩ (ଖ) ୧୦୪ (ଗ) ୧୪୨ (ଘ) ୧୫୬ (ଙ) ୧୭୦ ।
ରାହୁଲ ବଗିଚାରେ ଲଗାଇବା ପାଇଁ ୫୬ଟି ଗଛ ଆଣିଥିଲେ। କିଛି ଗଛ ଶୁଖିଯିବା ପରେ ୨୮ଟି ଗଛ ବଳିଲା। କେତୋଟି ଗଛ ଶୁଖିଗଲା?
ଏକ ଝିଣ୍ଟିକା ୭୭ ନମ୍ବର ମାଳିରେ ଅଛି। ସେ ୧୦ଟି ମାଳି ପଛକୁ ଡେଇଁଲେ କେଉଁ ସଂଖ୍ୟାରେ ପହଞ୍ଚିବ?
q_and_a.answer: ଝିଣ୍ଟିକାଟି ୬୭ ନମ୍ବର ମାଳିରେ ପହଞ୍ଚିବ (୭୭ - ୧୦ = ୬୭)।

q_and_a.question: ସଂଖ୍ୟାମାଳିରେ ଗୋଟିଏ ବେଙ୍ଗ ୭ ନମ୍ବର ମାଳିରେ ଅଛି। ସେ ଗୋଟିଏ ଥରରେ ୧୦ଟି ମାଳି ଆଗକୁ ଡେଇଁଲେ କେଉଁ ସଂଖ୍ୟାରେ ପହଞ୍ଚିବ?
q_and_a.answer: ବେଙ୍ଗଟି ୧୭ ନମ୍ବର ମାଳିରେ ପହଞ୍ଚିବ (୭ + ୧୦ = ୧୭)।

q_and_a.question: ଦୀପକ ୯ଟି କାହାଣୀ ପୁସ୍ତକ ଏବଂ ନନ୍ଦିନୀ ୭ଟି ଗାଣିତିକ ଧନ୍ଦା ପୁସ୍ତକ ଆଣିଥିଲେ। ସେମାନେ ଆଈ ମା'ଙ୍କ ପାଇଁ ମୋଟ କେତୋଟି ପୁସ୍ତକ ଆଣିଥିଲେ?
q_and_a.answer: ସେମାନେ ଆଈ ମା'ଙ୍କ ପାଇଁ ମୋଟ ୧୬ଟି ପୁସ୍ତକ ଆଣିଥିଲେ (୯ + ୭ = ୧୬)।

q_and_a.question: ଦୀପକ ଦୋକାନରୁ ୭ଟି ଜିଲାପି କିଣିଥିଲା ଏବଂ ଏବେ ତା' ପାଖରେ ୫ଟି ଅଛି। ନନ୍ଦିନୀ କେତୋଟି ଜିଲାପି ଖାଇଦେଇଥିଲା?
q_and_a.answer: ନନ୍ଦିନୀ ୨ଟି ଜିଲାପି ଖାଇଦେଇଥିଲା (୭ - ୫ = ୨)।

q_and_a.question: ନନ୍ଦିନୀର ବାକ୍ସରେ ୭ଟି ଜିଲାପି ଓ ଦୀପକର ବାକ୍ସରେ ୫ଟି ଜିଲାପି ଥିଲା। ଦୁହିଁଙ୍କ ପାଖରେ ମୋଟ କେତୋଟି ଜିଲାପି ଥିଲା?
କ୍ରିକେଟ ମ୍ୟାଚରେ ନେତାଜୀ କ୍ରିକେଟ ଟିମ୍ ମଧ୍ୟାହ୍ନ ଭୋଜନ ପୂର୍ବରୁ ୫୬ ରନ୍ ଓ ମଧ୍ୟାହ୍ନ ଭୋଜନ ପରେ ୭୫ ରନ୍ କଲେ। ସେମାନଙ୍କର ମୋଟ ରନ୍ ସଂଖ୍ୟା କେତେ?
ବବଲି ଦିଦି ସୋମବାର ୩୪ଟି ବହି ଓ ମଙ୍ଗଳବାର ୪୫ଟି ବହି ବିକ୍ରି କଲେ। ସେ ଦୁଇ ଦିନରେ ସମୁଦାୟ କେତେ ବହି ବିକ୍ରି କଲେ ଏବଂ ମଙ୍ଗଳବାର କେତେ ଅଧିକ ବହି ବିକ୍ରି ହେଲା?
q_and_a.answer: ଦୁଇ ଦିନରେ ସେ ସମୁଦାୟ ୭୯ଟି ବହି (୩୪ + ୪୫ = ୭୯) ବିକ୍ରି କଲେ ଏବଂ ମଙ୍ଗଳବାର ଦିନ ୧୧ଟି ଅଧିକ ବହି (୪୫ - ୩୪ = ୧୧) ବିକ୍ରି ହେଲା।

q_and_a.question: ନନ୍ଦିନୀ ୮୫ଟି ଏବଂ ଦୀପକ ୭୬ଟି ସେଓ ସଂଗ୍ରହ କରିଥିଲେ। ନନ୍ଦିନୀ, ଦୀପକଠାରୁ କେତୋଟି ଅଧିକ ସେଓ ସଂଗ୍ରହ କରିଥିଲା?
q_and_a.answer: ନନ୍ଦିନୀ, ଦୀପକଠାରୁ ୯ଟି ଅଧିକ ସେଓ ସଂଗ୍ରହ କରିଥିଲା (୮୫ - ୭୬ = ୯)।

q_and_a.question: ନନ୍ଦିନୀ ୮୫ଟି ଏବଂ ଦୀପକ ୭୬ଟି ସେଓ ତୋଳିଥିଲେ। ସେମାନେ ମୋଟରେ କେତୋଟି ସେଓ ସଂଗ୍ରହ କଲେ?
ଏକ ବାକ୍ସରେ ଥିବା ୧୦୦ଟି ପନିପରିବା ମଧ୍ୟରୁ ୭୫ଟି ଟମାଟୋ ହୋଇଥିଲେ, ଗାଜର ସଂଖ୍ୟା କେତେ ହେବ?
q_and_a.answer: ବାକ୍ସରେ ଗାଜର ସଂଖ୍ୟା ୨୫ଟି ହେବ। ଏହାକୁ ୧୦୦ - ୭୫ = ୨୫ ଭାବେ ଲେଖାଯାଇପାରିବ।

q_and_a.question: ଆଈ ମା' ୨୫ଟି ଲାଲ୍ ମୂଳା ଓ ୩୨ଟି ଧଳା ମୂଳା ଉପାଡ଼ି ଆଣିଲେ। କାଠି ବିଡ଼ା ସାହାଯ୍ୟରେ ସେମାନଙ୍କର ମୋଟ ସଂଖ୍ୟା କିପରି ହିସାବ କରାଯିବ?
q_and_a.answer: ୨୫ ପାଇଁ ୨ଟି ଦଶକ ବିଡ଼ା ଓ ୫ଟି ଖୋଲା କାଠି ଏବଂ ୩୨ ପାଇଁ ୩ଟି ଦଶକ ବିଡ଼ା ଓ ୨ଟି ଖୋଲା କାଠି ନିଆଯିବ। ମୋଟରେ ୫ଟି ବିଡ଼ା (୫୦) ଏବଂ ୭ଟି ଖୋଲା କାଠି ମିଶି ସମୁଦାୟ ୫୭ଟି ମୂଳା ହେବ।

q_and_a.question: ୭ ଡେଇଁ କ୍ରମରେ ୨୮ରୁ ଆରମ୍ଭ କରି ପରବର୍ତ୍ତୀ ତିନୋଟି ସଂଖ୍ୟା ଲେଖ।
q_and_a.answer: ୨୮ରୁ ୭ ଡେଇଁ ଆଗକୁ ଗଲେ ପରବର୍ତ୍ତୀ ତିନୋଟି ସଂଖ୍ୟା ହେବ ୩୫, ୪୨ ଏବଂ ୪୯।

q_and_a.question: ନନ୍ଦିନୀ ଓ ଦୀପକଙ୍କ ପାଖରେ ଥିବା ୫୨ଟି ଡାକ ଟିକେଟ୍ ମଧ୍ୟରୁ ୩୭ଟିରେ ବିଶିଷ୍ଟ ବ୍ୟକ୍ତିଙ୍କ ମୁହଁ ରହିଛି। ଅବଶିଷ୍ଟ ସ୍ମାରକୀ ଚିତ୍ର ଥିବା ଡାକ ଟିକେଟ୍ ସଂଖ୍ୟା କେତେ?
q_and_a.answer: ସ୍ମାରକୀ ଚିତ୍ର ଥିବା ଡାକ ଟିକେଟ୍ ସଂଖ୍ୟା ୧୫ଟି। ଏହା ୫୨ ରୁ ୩୭ ବିୟୋଗ କରି ନିର୍ଣ୍ଣୟ କରାଗଲା (୫୨ - ୩୭ = ୧୫)।

q_and_a.question: ନନ୍ଦିନୀ ଓ ଦୀପକ ପାଖରେ ୧୫ଟି ଡାକ ଟିକେଟ୍ ଥିଲା ଏବଂ ଆଈ ମା' ଆଉ ୭ଟି ଦେଲେ। ଦୀପକ ସଂଖ୍ୟା ମାଳ ବ୍ୟବହାର କରି କିପରି ଏହାର ଯୋଗଫଳ ବାହାର କରିଥିଲା?
q_and_a.answer: ଦୀପକ ପ୍ରଥମେ ୧୫ ସହିତ ୫ ଯୋଗ କରି ୨୦ ପାଇଲା। ତା'ପରେ ୨୦ ସହିତ ଆଉ ୨ ଯୋଗ କରି ମୋଟ ୨୨ଟି ଡାକ ଟିକେଟ୍ ବୋଲି ଉତ୍ତର ବାହାର କଲା।

q_and_a.question: ‘କୌତୁକିଆ ମିଶାଣ’ ଅଧ୍ୟାୟରେ ଥିବା ୩x୩ ମ୍ୟାଜିକ୍ ବର୍ଗର ନିୟମ ବୁଝାଅ ଏବଂ ୧ ରୁ ୯ ସଂଖ୍ୟା ବ୍ୟବହାର କରି କିପରି ସବୁ ପାର୍ଶ୍ୱର ଯୋଗଫଳ ୧୫ ହୁଏ, ତାହା ଉଦାହରଣ ସହ ଦର୍ଶାଅ।
q_and_a.answer: ମ୍ୟାଜିକ୍ ବର୍ଗର ନିୟମ : ଏଥିରେ ୧ ରୁ ୯ ପର୍ଯ୍ୟନ୍ତ ପ୍ରତ୍ୟେକ ସଂଖ୍ୟାକୁ ଥରେ ଲେଖାଏଁ ବ୍ୟବହାର କରାଯାଏ। ଏହି ସଂଖ୍ୟାଗୁଡ଼ିକୁ ଏପରି ଭାବରେ ସଜାଇ ଲେଖାଯାଏ ଯେପରି ପ୍ରତ୍ୟେକ ଧାଡ଼ି (ବାମରୁ ଡାହାଣ), ପ୍ରତ୍ୟେକ ସ୍ତମ୍ଭ (ଉପରୁ ତଳ) ଏବଂ ପ୍ରତ୍ୟେକ କୋଣ ଅନୁକୋଣ (କର୍ଣ୍ଣ) ର ଯୋଗଫଳ ସର୍ବଦା ୧୫ ହେବ। ମ୍ୟାଜିକ୍ ବର୍ଗର ସଜାଣି : ପ୍ରଥମ ଧାଡ଼ି : ୨, ୭, ୬ ଦ୍ୱିତୀୟ ଧାଡ଼ି : ୯, ୫, ୧ ତୃତୀୟ ଧାଡ଼ି : ୪, ୩, ୮ ସମସ୍ତ ଦିଗରୁ ଯୋଗଫଳ ଯାଞ୍ଚ : ୧. ଧାଡ଼ି ଅନୁଯାୟୀ (ବାମରୁ ଡାହାଣ) : • ପ୍ରଥମ ଧାଡ଼ି : ୨ + ୭ + ୬ = ୧୫ • ଦ୍ୱିତୀୟ ଧାଡ଼ି : ୯ + ୫ + ୧ = ୧୫ • ତୃତୀୟ ଧାଡ଼ି : ୪ + ୩ + ୮ = ୧୫ ୨. ସ୍ତମ୍ଭ ଅନୁଯାୟୀ (ଉପରୁ ତଳ) : • ପ୍ରଥମ ସ୍ତମ୍ଭ : ୨ + ୯ + ୪ = ୧୫ • ଦ୍ୱିତୀୟ ସ୍ତମ୍ଭ : ୭ + ୫ + ୩ = ୧୫ • ତୃତୀୟ ସ୍ତମ୍ଭ : ୬ + ୧ + ୮ = ୧୫ ୩. କୋଣ ଅନୁକୋଣ ଅନୁଯାୟୀ (କର୍ଣ୍ଣ) : • ପ୍ରଥମ କର୍ଣ୍ଣ : ୨ + ୫ + ୮ = ୧୫ • ଦ୍ୱିତୀୟ କର୍ଣ୍ଣ : ୬ + ୫ + ୪ = ୧୫ ଏହିପରି ଭାବରେ ସବୁ ଦିଗରୁ ମିଶାଇଲେ ଯୋଗଫଳ ସର୍ବଦା ୧୫ ହୋଇଥାଏ।

q_and_a.question: ନନ୍ଦିନୀ ଗଛରୁ ୮୫ଟି ଏବଂ ଦୀପକ ୭୬ଟି ସେଓ ତୋଳିଲେ। (କ) ସେମାନେ ମୋଟ କେତୋଟି ସେଓ ସଂଗ୍ରହ କଲେ? (ଖ) କିଏ ଅଧିକ ସେଓ ତୋଳିଥିଲା ଏବଂ କେତୋଟି ଅଧିକ? କାଠି ବିଡ଼ା ଓ ସଂଖ୍ୟା ମାଧ୍ୟମରେ ବୁଝାଅ।
q_and_a.answer: (କ) ମୋଟ ସେଓ ସଂଖ୍ୟା ନିର୍ଣ୍ଣୟ : ନନ୍ଦିନୀର ସେଓ = ୮୫ ଟି ଦୀପକର ସେଓ = ୭୬ ଟି ସମୁଦାୟ ସେଓ = ୮୫ + ୭୬ କାଠି ବିଡ଼ା ସାହାଯ୍ୟରେ : ୮୫ = ୮ ଟି ବିଡ଼ା + ୫ ଟି ଖୋଲା କାଠି ୭୬ = ୭ ଟି ବିଡ଼ା + ୬ ଟି ଖୋଲା କାଠି ବିଡ଼ା ସଂଖ୍ୟା = ୮ + ୭ = ୧୫ ଟି ବିଡ଼ା (୧୫୦) ଖୋଲା କାଠି = ୫ + ୬ = ୧୧ ଟି (୧ ଟି ବିଡ଼ା + ୧ ଟି ଖୋଲା କାଠି = ୧୧) ମୋଟ ସେଓ = ୧୫୦ + ୧୧ = ୧୬୧ ଟି। ତେଣୁ ସେମାନେ ମୋଟ ୧୬୧ଟି ସେଓ ସଂଗ୍ରହ କଲେ। (ଖ) କିଏ କେତେ ଅଧିକ ସେଓ ତୋଳିଲା : ନନ୍ଦିନୀ ୮୫ଟି ସେଓ ତୋଳିଥିଲା ଏବଂ ଦୀପକ ୭୬ଟି ସେଓ ତୋଳିଥିଲା। ୮୫ ସଂଖ୍ୟାଟି ୭୬ ଠାରୁ ବଡ଼, ତେଣୁ ନନ୍ଦିନୀ ଅଧିକ ସେଓ ତୋଳିଥିଲା। ଅଧିକ ସେଓ ସଂଖ୍ୟା = ୮୫ - ୭୬ = ୯ ଟି। ତେଣୁ ନନ୍ଦିନୀ, ଦୀପକ ଠାରୁ ୯ଟି ଅଧିକ ସେଓ ତୋଳିଥିଲା।

q_and_a.question: ନନ୍ଦିନୀ ଏବଂ ଦୀପକଙ୍କ ପାଖରେ ୧୫ଟି ଡାକ ଟିକେଟ୍ ଥିଲା। ଆଈ ମା' ସେମାନଙ୍କୁ ଆଉ ୭ଟି ଡାକ ଟିକେଟ୍ ଦେଲେ। ଏବେ ସେମାନଙ୍କ ପାଖରେ ମୋଟ କେତୋଟି ଡାକ ଟିକେଟ୍ ହେଲା? ନନ୍ଦିନୀ, ଦୀପକ ଏବଂ ଆଈ ମା' ସଂଖ୍ୟା ମାଳ ବ୍ୟବହାର କରି ଏହାକୁ କିପରି ତିନୋଟି ଭିନ୍ନ ଉପାୟରେ ସମାଧାନ କରିଥିଲେ ବୁଝାଇ ଲେଖ।
q_and_a.answer: ମୋଟ ଡାକ ଟିକେଟ୍ ସଂଖ୍ୟା ନିର୍ଣ୍ଣୟ କରିବା ପାଇଁ ୧୫ ସହିତ ୭ ଯୋଗ କରିବାକୁ ହେବ। ଗାଣିତିକ ରୂପ : ୧୫ + ୭ = ୨୨ ସଂଖ୍ୟା ମାଳ ବ୍ୟବହାର କରି ତିନୋଟି ଭିନ୍ନ ଉପାୟରେ ସମାଧାନ : ୧. ନନ୍ଦିନୀର ଉପାୟ : ନନ୍ଦିନୀ ୧୫ ରୁ ଆରମ୍ଭ କରି ଏକ ଏକ କରି ୭ ଥର ଆଗକୁ ଗଣିଲା। ୧୫ ରୁ ୧୬, ୧୭, ୧୮, ୧୯, ୨୦, ୨୧, ୨୨। ଏହିପରି ସେ ୨୨ ପାଇଲା। ୨. ଦୀପକର ଉପାୟ : ଦୀପକ ପ୍ରଥମେ ୧୫ ସହିତ ୫ ଯୋଗ କରି ୨୦ କଲା। ତା'ପରେ ୨୦ ସହିତ ବଳକା ୨ ଯୋଗ କରି ୨୨ ପାଇଲା (୧୫ + ୫ = ୨୦, ୨୦ + ୨ = ୨୨)। ୩. ଆଈ ମା'ଙ୍କ ଉପାୟ : ଆଈ ମା' ପ୍ରଥମେ ୧୫ ସହିତ ୧୦ ଯୋଗ କରି ୨୫ କଲେ। ତା'ପରେ ୨୫ ରୁ ୩ ବିୟୋଗ କରି ୨୨ ପାଇଲେ (୧୫ + ୧୦ = ୨୫, ୨୫ - ୩ = ୨୨)। ଏହିପରି ତିନୋଟି ଯାକ ଉପାୟରେ ସମାନ ଉତ୍ତର ମିଳିଲା। ତେଣୁ ସେମାନଙ୍କ ପାଖରେ ସମୁଦାୟ ୨୨ଟି ଡାକ ଟିକେଟ୍ ହେଲା।

q_and_a.question: (କ) ୧ ରୁ ୧୦୦ ସଂଖ୍ୟା ସାରଣୀ ବ୍ୟବହାର କରି ନିମ୍ନଲିଖିତ ଯୋଗଗୁଡ଼ିକୁ ଦଶକ ଓ ଏକକ ଡେଇଁବା କୌଶଳରେ ବୁଝାଅ : (i) ୨୩ + ୧୧ = ? (ii) ୧୯ + ୫୪ = ? (ଖ) ନିମ୍ନଲିଖିତ ଗାଣିତିକ ପ୍ରକ୍ରିୟାଗୁଡ଼ିକର ଫଳାଫଳ ‘୧୦୦ ରୁ ଅଧିକ’ କିମ୍ବା ‘୧୦୦ ରୁ କମ୍’ ହେବ, ତାହା କାରଣ ସହ ନିର୍ଣ୍ଣୟ କର : (i) ୭୦ + ୪୧ (ii) ୧୪୦ - ୪୯ (iii) ୧୯୯ - ୮୦ (iv) ୭୮ - ୨୬
q_and_a.answer: (କ) ସଂଖ୍ୟା ସାରଣୀରେ ଯୋଗ କରିବା କୌଶଳ : (i) ୨୩ + ୧୧ : • ପ୍ରଥମେ ସଂଖ୍ୟା ସାରଣୀରେ ୨୩ ରେ ରହିବା। • ୧୧ କୁ ୧୦ + ୧ ଭାବେ ଭାଙ୍ଗିବା। • ୨୩ ରୁ ୧୦ ଆଗକୁ (୧ ଧାଡ଼ି ତଳକୁ) ଗଲେ ୩୩ ହୁଏ। • ୩୩ ରୁ ଆଉ ୧ ଘର ଡାହାଣକୁ ଗଲେ ୩୪ ହୁଏ। • ତେଣୁ ୨୩ + ୧୧ = ୩୪। (ii) ୧୯ + ୫୪ : • ପ୍ରଥମେ ସଂଖ୍ୟା ସାରଣୀରେ ୧୯ ରେ ରହିବା। • ୫୪ କୁ ୫୦ + ୪ ଭାବେ ଭାଙ୍ଗିବା। • ୧୯ ରୁ ୫୦ ଆଗକୁ (୫ ଧାଡ଼ି ତଳକୁ) ଗଲେ ୬୯ ହୁଏ। • ୬୯ ରୁ ଆଉ ୪ ଘର ଡାହାଣକୁ ଗଲେ ୭୩ ହୁଏ। • ତେଣୁ ୧୯ + ୫୪ = ୭୩। (ଖ) ‘୧୦୦ ରୁ ଅଧିକ’ କିମ୍ବା ‘୧୦୦ ରୁ କମ୍’ ନିର୍ଣ୍ଣୟ : (i) ୭୦ + ୪୧ : ୭୦ ସହିତ ୩୦ ମିଶିଲେ ୧୦୦ ହୁଏ। ଏଠାରେ ୪୧ ଯୋଡ଼ା ଯାଉଛି, ଯାହା ୩୦ ଠାରୁ ବଡ଼। ତେଣୁ ଯୋଗଫଳ (୧୧୧) ‘୧୦୦ ରୁ ଅଧିକ’ ହେବ। (ii) ୧୪୦ - ୪୯ : ୧୪୦ ରୁ ୪୦ ବିୟୋଗ କଲେ ୧୦୦ ହୁଏ। ଏଠାରେ ୪୦ ଠାରୁ ଅଧିକ (୪୯) ବିୟୋଗ କରାଯାଉଛି। ତେଣୁ ବିୟୋଗଫଳ (୯୧) ‘୧୦୦ ରୁ କମ୍’ ହେବ। (iii) ୧୯୯ - ୮୦ : ୧୯୯ ରୁ ୮୦ ବିୟୋଗ କଲେ ୧୧୯ ମିଳେ। ୧୧୯ ସଂଖ୍ୟାଟି ୧୦୦ ଠାରୁ ବଡ଼, ତେଣୁ ଏହାର ଫଳାଫଳ ‘୧୦୦ ରୁ ଅଧିକ’ ହେବ। (iv) ୭୮ - ୨୬ : ୭୮ ସଂଖ୍ୟାଟି ନିଜେ ୧୦୦ ଠାରୁ କମ୍। ସେଥିରୁ ୨୬ ବିୟୋଗ କଲେ ବିୟୋଗଫଳ (୫୨) ନିଶ୍ଚିତ ଭାବେ ‘୧୦୦ ରୁ କମ୍’ ହେବ।

q_and_a.question: ନିମ୍ନଲିଖିତ ଦୈନନ୍ଦିନ ଗାଣିତିକ ସମସ୍ୟାଗୁଡ଼ିକର ସମାଧାନ ପଦ୍ଧତି ଅନୁଯାୟୀ କର : (କ) ବବଲି ଦିଦି ସୋମବାର ୩୪ଟି ବହି ଓ ମଙ୍ଗଳବାର ୪୫ଟି ବହି ବିକ୍ରି କରିଛନ୍ତି। ଦୁଇ ଦିନରେ ସେ ମୋଟ କେତୋଟି ବହି ବିକ୍ରି କଲେ? ମଙ୍ଗଳବାର ସେ ସୋମବାର ତୁଳନାରେ କେତୋଟି ଅଧିକ ବହି ବିକ୍ରି କରିଛନ୍ତି? (ଖ) ଏକ କ୍ରିକେଟ ମ୍ୟାଚରେ ନେତାଜୀ କ୍ରିକେଟ ଟିମ୍ ମଧ୍ୟାହ୍ନ ଭୋଜନ ପୂର୍ବରୁ ୫୬ ରନ୍ ଓ ମଧ୍ୟାହ୍ନ ଭୋଜନ ପରେ ୭୫ ରନ୍ କରିଥିଲେ। ସେମାନେ ସମୁଦାୟ କେତେ ରନ୍ କଲେ? (ଗ) ରାହୁଲ ବଗିଚାରେ ଲଗାଇବା ପାଇଁ ୫୬ଟି ଗଛ ଆଣିଥିଲେ। ସେଥିରୁ କିଛି ଗଛ ଶୁଖିଗଲା ଏବଂ ତାଙ୍କ ପାଖରେ ଆଉ ୨୮ଟି ଗଛ ରହିଲା। ତେବେ କେତୋଟି ଗଛ ଶୁଖିଗଲା?
